crop_layers.tooltip: Geometry of the layers/masks batch outputs (layer_stack is unaffected and always tight). Full canvas: each layer on a base-sized canvas at its bounding-box position - recompose directly with ImageCompositeMasked. Minimal size: each layer cropped to its bounding box (padded to the largest layer for batching) - much smaller tensors; rebuild placement with Layers From Bounding Boxes using the bboxes output.

output_tooltips: The base image (background plate) the layers stack onto.
Transparency of the base image (1 = transparent, LoadImage convention); currently always fully opaque.

Transparent layers ordered bottom to top. Full canvas mode: placed on a black base-sized canvas at their bounding-box position. Minimal size mode: cropped to their bounding box, anchored top-left, padded to the largest layer.
Per-layer transparency, index-aligned with the layers batch (1 = transparent, LoadImage convention). For ImageCompositeMasked-style compositing, add InvertMask first.

One placement box per layer, index-aligned with the layers batch (feed both, plus masks, into Layers From Bounding Boxes to rebuild per-layer placement): {x, y, width, height, metadata: {name, desc, z_index, native_size, content_rect, flags}}. content_rect = [left, top, width, height] is the layer's content region within its own frame; it lands on the canvas at the box position plus that offset.

Ready-to-edit layer document for Create Layered Image: the base plate plus each element as its own named, tight-cropped layer at its true position and stacking order. Connect directly, or extend with Add Layer.

text_prompt.tooltip: Describe the voice(s), emotion, pacing, ambience, background music and sound effects, and include the lines to speak (name characters inline for dialogue). In 'audio reference' mode, refer to connected clips by order as @Audio1, @Audio2, @Audio3. With the multilingual model, a quoted line can start with a timestamp range that controls when and how long it is spoken, e.g. "[5.5s:8.0s] Wait for me!". Write the prompt in the same language as the lines to speak. Maximum 3000 characters.

reference_mode.tooltip: How to condition the voice: 'text only' (describe everything in the prompt), 'audio reference' (clone up to 3 voices, tagged @Audio1-3), 'image reference' (derive a voice from one character image), or 'preset voice' (pick a built-in named voice that reads the prompt).

reference_audio_1.tooltip: Reference clip for voice cloning, tagged @Audio1 in the prompt. Up to 30s.

reference_audio_2.tooltip: Reference clip tagged @Audio2 in the prompt. Up to 30s.

reference_audio_3.tooltip: Reference clip tagged @Audio3 in the prompt. Up to 30s.

reference_image.tooltip: A single character image; the model derives a voice from it. Cannot be combined with reference audio.

preset_voice.tooltip: A built-in TTS 2.0 voice that reads the prompt. No reference clip needed, and @AudioN tags are not used in this mode.

seed.tooltip: Seed controls whether the node should re-run; results are non-deterministic regardless of seed.

model.tooltip: seed-audio-1.0-multilingual: 20 languages (English, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Mexican & Castilian Spanish, Indonesian, German, Brazilian Portuguese, French, Thai, Vietnamese, Malay, Filipino, Italian, Russian, Dutch, Polish, Turkish, Swedish) plus per-sentence timing control via "[5.5s:8.0s] ..." timestamps. seed-audio-1.0: English and Chinese only, no timing control.

ByteDanceSeedAudio.name: ByteDanceSeedAudio
ByteDanceSeedAudio.description: Generate speech, music, sound effects and multi-speaker dialogue from a single prompt with ByteDance Seed Audio 1.0. Describe the voice(s), emotion, ambience, background music and sound effects in the prompt, and include the lines to speak. Optionally pick a built-in preset voice, clone voices from up to 3 reference clips (tagged @Audio1-3 in the prompt), or derive a voice from a character image. Up to 2 minutes of audio per run. The multilingual model supports 20 languages and timestamp-based timing control.

video.tooltip: Video to enhance. The source resolution must be at most 2560x1440 (2K); the output size is set by the resolution input.

tool_version.tooltip: 'standard' balances speed and quality with 10+ enhancement algorithms. 'professional' uses 30+ algorithms for cinema-grade restoration, takes about 3x longer and costs 10x more.

scene.tooltip: Preset tuned to the content: 'aigc' for AI-generated footage, 'common' for general video, 'ugc' for compressed phone clips, 'short_series' for drama with faces, 'old_film' for scratched or flickering archive footage.

enhance_style.tooltip: 'hd' applies a sharper enhancement; 'natural' reduces the strength for a softer, less sharpened look.
'hd' applies a sharper enhancement; 'natural' reduces the strength for a softer, less sharpened look.

resolution.tooltip: Output resolution. The short side is set to the chosen level and the long side follows the source aspect ratio. 'source' keeps the source size, 'custom' sets the short side in pixels. Sources wider or taller than about 2.2:1 are billed one resolution tier higher.

short_side.tooltip: Short side of the output in pixels; the long side follows the source aspect ratio.

fps.tooltip: Output frame rate. A higher rate than the source enables AI frame interpolation; a lower one drops frames. 'source' keeps the source rate, up to 120 fps. Rates above 30 fps cost 2x, above 60 fps 4x.

bitrate_level.tooltip: Target bitrate of the delivered file, scaled to the output resolution and frame rate.

system_prompt.tooltip: Foundational instructions that dictate an AI's behavior.
system_prompt.default:
You are an expert image-generation engine. You must ALWAYS produce an image.
Interpret all user input—regardless of format, intent, or abstraction—as literal visual directives for image composition.
If a prompt is conversational or lacks specific visual details, you must creatively invent a concrete visual scenario that depicts the concept.
Prioritize generating the visual representation above any text, formatting, or conversational requests.

height.tooltip: Used only when resolution is 'custom'. Must be a multiple of 16; the total pixel area can be up to 4096x4096. Any aspect ratio works; beyond about 6:1 the model starts repeating the subject.

seed.tooltip: Seed to use for generation; results still vary between runs with the same seed.

reference_detail.tooltip: How much detail of the reference images the model sees: 'standard' is up to 1024x1024 pixels per image, 'high' is up to 2048x2048 and preserves small text and fine detail better, but takes longer.

watermark.tooltip: Whether to add an AI-generated watermark to the result.

IdeogramV4.name: IdeogramV4
IdeogramV4.description: Generates images using the Ideogram 4.0 model from a text prompt.

prompt.tooltip: Text prompt. Also accepts an Ideogram 4.0 structured JSON caption (exact colors as #RRGGBB hexes, exact text strings, bounding-box layout) — set prompt_upsampling to OFF to use it verbatim.

quality.tooltip: Speed/price/quality tier. MEDIUM is the everyday default; HIGH for complex prompts, fine detail and difficult text; VERY_LOW/LOW for drafts at scale. Difficult text renders poorly below MEDIUM.

resolution.tooltip: Output size class (exact pixels follow the aspect ratio, e.g. 16:9 gives 1280x720 at 1K and 2560x1440 at 2K). Prefer HIGH + 2K for crisp typography.

aspect_ratio.tooltip: The aspect ratio for image generation.

prompt_upsampling.tooltip: Expands short prompts into a detailed structured caption before generation (the rewritten prompt is returned as final_prompt). Set OFF when supplying your own JSON caption or exact wording.

seed.tooltip: Seed for reproducible generation. With prompt_upsampling OFF, the same seed and settings return the same image; with ON/AUTO the prompt rewrite varies per run — reproduce a result by reusing its final_prompt output with prompt_upsampling OFF and the same seed.

output_tooltips: The prompt the image was actually generated from (the rewritten structured caption when prompt_upsampling ran, else your prompt). Feed it back with prompt_upsampling OFF and the same seed to reproduce this image.
IdeogramPImage.name: IdeogramPImage
IdeogramPImage.description: Generates images using P-Image, Ideogram's fast text-to-image model. Strong typography and photorealism; supports Ideogram 4.0 structured JSON captions for exact text, colors and layout.

model.tooltip: Model to use.

prompt.tooltip: Text prompt. Also accepts an Ideogram structured JSON caption, for example a previous final_prompt.

size.tooltip: Output size. 'auto' lets the model pick a canvas that suits the prompt.

quality.tooltip: Quality tier. Higher tiers cost more and take longer.

magic_prompt.tooltip: Rewrites the prompt into a detailed structured caption before generating; 'off' keeps your wording as literal as possible. The caption is returned as final_prompt.

seed.tooltip: Seed for generation. Text-to-image is not reproducible from the seed alone because the prompt is rewritten on every run; to reproduce an image, reuse its final_prompt with magic_prompt set to 'off' and the same seed.

output_tooltips: The structured caption the image was generated from. Feed it back with magic_prompt set to 'off' and the same seed to reproduce the image.

RunwayAleph2VideoToVideoNode.name: RunwayAleph2VideoToVideoNode
RunwayAleph2VideoToVideoNode.description: Edit a video with a text prompt using Runway's Aleph2 model. Aleph2 transforms your footage (restyle, relight, add or remove elements, change the viewpoint) while keeping the original motion and timing; the output resolution matches the input video, which must be 2-30 seconds at 30 fps or lower. Optionally steer the edit with either keyframes (anchored to the input video) or prompt images (anchored to the output video) - use one or the other, not both.

keyframes.tooltip: Optional earlier keyframes to chain with this one.

Connect this to the 'keyframes' input of the Runway Aleph2 Video to Video node; chain several together (up to 5) via the optional 'keyframes' input below.

sync_mode.tooltip: How to handle a duration mismatch between video and audio; this also sets the output length. bounce: video plays forward then backward until the audio ends (output = audio length). loop: video restarts until the audio ends (output = audio length). remap: video is time-stretched to match the audio (output = audio length). cut_off: the longer track is trimmed (output = shorter length). silence: nothing is trimmed; the shorter track is padded (output = longer length).

speaker_selection.tooltip: Which face to lipsync when several people are visible. default: let the model decide. auto-detect: detect and follow the active speaker. coordinates: target the face at pixel (speaker_x, speaker_y) in the frame chosen by speaker_frame.

speaker_frame.tooltip: Video frame used to locate the speaker. Only used when speaker_selection is 'coordinates'.

speaker_x.tooltip: X pixel coordinate of the speaker's face. Only used when speaker_selection is 'coordinates'.

speaker_y.tooltip: Y pixel coordinate of the speaker's face. Only used when speaker_selection is 'coordinates'.

seed.tooltip: Seed controls whether the node should re-run; results are non-deterministic regardless of seed.

speaker_selection.tooltip: Which face to animate when several people are visible. default: let the model decide. coordinates: target the face at pixel (speaker_x, speaker_y) in the image. Auto-detection is not supported for images.

speaker_x.tooltip: X pixel coordinate of the speaker's face. Only used when speaker_selection is 'coordinates'.

speaker_y.tooltip: Y pixel coordinate of the speaker's face. Only used when speaker_selection is 'coordinates'.

auto_downscale.tooltip: Automatically downscale the image if it exceeds the 4K (4096x2160) input limit; speaker coordinates are scaled to match. When disabled, an oversized image raises an error instead.

Basic data handling: Boolean And.name: Basic data handling: Boolean And
Basic data handling: Boolean And.description:
Returns the logical AND (conjunction) of two boolean values.

Outputs True only when both inputs are True. This matches the behaviour of the
Python ``and`` operator applied to the two operands.
output_tooltips: True only when both inputs are True, otherwise False.

invert.tooltip: When enabled, negates the result (turns AND into NAND).

item_0.tooltip: One of the values to combine. Connect more values to add operands.

Basic data handling: Generic And.name: Basic data handling: Generic And
Basic data handling: Generic And.description:
Returns the AND of any number of values, evaluated with Python truthiness.

Connect additional values to the dynamic item input to add more operands. Because
Python truthiness is used, values such as ``0``, ``""``, ``[]``, ``{}`` and ``None``
count as False. When *invert* is enabled the result is negated (NAND).
output_tooltips: True when all connected values are truthy (unless inverted).

Basic data handling: Boolean Nand.name: Basic data handling: Boolean Nand
Basic data handling: Boolean Nand.description:
Returns the logical NAND of two boolean values.

Outputs False only when both inputs are True; it is the negation of AND.
output_tooltips: False only when both inputs are True, otherwise True.

Basic data handling: Boolean Nor.name: Basic data handling: Boolean Nor
Basic data handling: Boolean Nor.description:
Returns the logical NOR of two boolean values.

Outputs True only when both inputs are False; it is the negation of OR.
output_tooltips: True only when both inputs are False, otherwise False.

input.tooltip: The value to negate.

Basic data handling: Boolean Not.name: Basic data handling: Boolean Not
Basic data handling: Boolean Not.description:
Returns the logical NOT (negation) of a boolean value.

Outputs True when the input is False and False when the input is True.
output_tooltips: True when the input is False, False when the input is True.

Basic data handling: Boolean Or.name: Basic data handling: Boolean Or
Basic data handling: Boolean Or.description:
Returns the logical OR (disjunction) of two boolean values.

Outputs True when at least one input is True. This matches the behaviour of the
Python ``or`` operator applied to the two operands.
output_tooltips: True when at least one input is True, otherwise False.

invert.tooltip: When enabled, negates the result (turns OR into NOR).

item_0.tooltip: One of the values to combine. Connect more values to add operands.

Basic data handling: Generic Or.name: Basic data handling: Generic Or
Basic data handling: Generic Or.description:
Returns the OR of any number of values, evaluated with Python truthiness.

Connect additional values to the dynamic item input to add more operands. Because
Python truthiness is used, values such as ``0``, ``""``, ``[]``, ``{}`` and ``None``
count as False. When *invert* is enabled the result is negated (NOR).
output_tooltips: True when at least one connected value is truthy (unless inverted).

Basic data handling: Boolean Xor.name: Basic data handling: Boolean Xor
Basic data handling: Boolean Xor.description:
Returns the logical XOR (exclusive or) of two boolean values.

Outputs True when the inputs differ from one another and False when they are equal.
output_tooltips: True when the two inputs differ, False when they are equal.

input.tooltip: The value to convert to a BOOLEAN.

Basic data handling: CastToBoolean.name: Basic data handling: CastToBoolean
output_tooltips: The input value converted to a BOOLEAN.

input.tooltip: The value to convert to a DICT.

Basic data handling: CastToDict.name: Basic data handling: CastToDict
Basic data handling: CastToDict.description:
Converts a value into a DICT.

The input must already be a mapping, or an iterable of key-value pairs (for
example a LIST of two-element sequences such as ``[["a", 1], ["b", 2]]``).
Raises a ValueError for any other kind of input.
output_tooltips: The input value converted to a DICT.

input.tooltip: The value to convert to a FLOAT.

Basic data handling: CastToFloat.name: Basic data handling: CastToFloat
Basic data handling: CastToFloat.description:
Converts a numeric value to a FLOAT.

Accepts INT, FLOAT and numeric strings such as ``"3.14"``. Values that cannot be
parsed as a number raise a ValueError.
output_tooltips: The input value converted to a FLOAT.

input.tooltip: The value to convert to an INT.

Basic data handling: CastToInt.name: Basic data handling: CastToInt
Basic data handling: CastToInt.description:
Converts a numeric value to an INT, truncating toward zero.

Accepts INT, FLOAT (fractional part is dropped, like ``int()``) and numeric strings
such as ``"42"``. Values that cannot be converted raise a ValueError.
output_tooltips: The input value converted to an INT.

input.tooltip: The value to convert to a LIST.

Basic data handling: CastToList.name: Basic data handling: CastToList
output_tooltips: The input value converted to a LIST.

input.tooltip: The value to convert to a SET.

Basic data handling: CastToSet.name: Basic data handling: CastToSet
Basic data handling: CastToSet.description:
Converts a value into a SET (an unordered collection of unique items).

Sets are returned unchanged; a list or ComfyUI data list becomes the set of its
items (duplicates removed); any other single value is wrapped into a one-element set.
output_tooltips: The input value converted to a SET.

input.tooltip: The value to convert to a STRING.

Basic data handling: CastToString.name: Basic data handling: CastToString
Basic data handling: CastToString.description:
Converts any value to a STRING using its textual representation.

Numbers, booleans, lists, dicts, sets and other values are rendered with ``str()``,
matching Python's default formatting.
output_tooltips: The input value converted to a STRING.

Basic data handling: Equal.name: Basic data handling: Equal
Basic data handling: Equal.description:
Checks if two values are equal.

This node takes two inputs of any type and returns True if they are equal,
and False otherwise. For complex objects (lists, dicts, sets), structural
equality is tested.
output_tooltips: True when the two values are equal, otherwise False.

Basic data handling: NotEqual.name: Basic data handling: NotEqual
Basic data handling: NotEqual.description:
Checks if two values are not equal.

This node takes two inputs of any type and returns True if they are not equal,
and False otherwise. For complex objects (lists, dicts, sets), structural
inequality is tested.
output_tooltips: True when the two values are not equal, otherwise False.

Basic data handling: LessThan.name: Basic data handling: LessThan
Basic data handling: LessThan.description:
Checks if the first value is less than the second.

This node takes two numerical inputs and returns True if the first value
is strictly less than the second value, and False otherwise.
output_tooltips: True when value1 is strictly less than value2, otherwise False.

Basic data handling: LessThanOrEqual.name: Basic data handling: LessThanOrEqual
Basic data handling: LessThanOrEqual.description:
Checks if the first value is less than or equal to the second.

This node takes two numerical inputs and returns True if the first value
is less than or equal to the second value, and False otherwise.
output_tooltips: True when value1 is less than or equal to value2, otherwise False.

Basic data handling: GreaterThan.name: Basic data handling: GreaterThan
Basic data handling: GreaterThan.description:
Checks if the first value is greater than the second.

This node takes two numerical inputs and returns True if the first value
is strictly greater than the second value, and False otherwise.
output_tooltips: True when value1 is strictly greater than value2, otherwise False.

Basic data handling: GreaterThanOrEqual.name: Basic data handling: GreaterThanOrEqual
Basic data handling: GreaterThanOrEqual.description:
Checks if the first value is greater than or equal to the second.

This node takes two numerical inputs and returns True if the first value
is greater than or equal to the second value, and False otherwise.
output_tooltips: True when value1 is greater than or equal to value2, otherwise False.

value.tooltip: The value to test for null.

Basic data handling: IsNull.name: Basic data handling: IsNull
Basic data handling: IsNull.description:
Checks if a value is None/null.

This node takes any input value and returns True if the value is None
(Python null), and False otherwise.
output_tooltips: True when the input value is None, otherwise False.

value.tooltip: The number to test.

include_min.tooltip: Treat the lower bound as inside the range (>=).

include_max.tooltip: Treat the upper bound as inside the range (<=).

Basic data handling: NumberInRange.name: Basic data handling: NumberInRange
Basic data handling: NumberInRange.description:
Checks if a number is within a specified range.

This node takes a number, a minimum and a maximum bound, and returns True if the
number lies within the range. The ``include_min`` and ``include_max`` options control
whether the boundaries themselves count as being inside the range.
output_tooltips: True when the number lies within the configured range.

container.tooltip: The object whose length is measured (string, list, dict, set, ...).

operator.tooltip: Comparison operator applied between the length and the given value.

length.tooltip: The value the measured length is compared against.

Basic data handling: CompareLength.name: Basic data handling: CompareLength
Basic data handling: CompareLength.description:
Compares the length of a container (string, list, dict, set, ...) with a value.

This node measures ``len(container)`` and compares it with *length* using the
selected *operator*. Returns the boolean result and, as a convenience, the
actual measured length.
output_tooltips: Result of evaluating length <operator> value.
The measured length of the container (-1 when it has no length).

operator.tooltip: Comparison operator applied between the two strings.

case_sensitive.tooltip: When enabled, letter case is respected (e.g. 'A' != 'a').

Basic data handling: StringComparison.name: Basic data handling: StringComparison
Basic data handling: StringComparison.description:
Compares two strings using a selected comparison operator.

This node takes two string inputs and an operator, and returns True when the
comparison holds. Comparisons are lexicographic (dictionary order); enable
*case_sensitive* to treat uppercase and lowercase letters as distinct.
output_tooltips: True when the selected comparison holds between the two strings.

if_true.tooltip: Value returned when the condition is True.

if_false.tooltip: Value returned when the condition is False.

Basic data handling: IfElse.name: Basic data handling: IfElse
Basic data handling: IfElse.description:
Implements a conditional branch (if/else) in the workflow.

This node takes a condition input and two value inputs. If the condition
evaluates to True, the first value is returned; otherwise, the second value
is returned. This allows conditional data flow in ComfyUI workflows.
output_tooltips: The value of the branch selected by the condition.

if.tooltip: Main condition; when True the 'then' value is returned.

then.tooltip: Value returned when the 'if' condition is True.

elif_0.tooltip: Optional else-if condition. Connect more to chain additional branches.

then_0.tooltip: Value returned when the matching elif_<n> condition is True.

else.tooltip: Value returned when no condition is True.

Basic data handling: IfElifElse.name: Basic data handling: IfElifElse
Basic data handling: IfElifElse.description:
Implements a conditional branch (if/elif/else) in the workflow.

This node takes a condition input and two value inputs. If the condition
evaluates to True, the first value is returned; otherwise, the elif (else if)
is evaluated and returned when true. This continues for all additional elifs.
When none is true, the value of the else is returned.
This allows conditional data flow in ComfyUI workflows.
output_tooltips: The value of the first branch whose condition is True (or the else value).

select.tooltip: Zero-based index of the case to select.

case_0.tooltip: Value returned when its index is selected. Connect more values to add cases.

default.tooltip: Value returned when the selected index is out of range.

Basic data handling: SwitchCase.name: Basic data handling: SwitchCase
Basic data handling: SwitchCase.description:
Implements a switch/case selection in the workflow.

This node takes a selector input (an integer) and multiple case value inputs.
It returns the value corresponding to the provided index. If the index is out
of range, the default value is returned. This allows for selection from multiple
options based on a computed index.

NOTE: This version of the node will most likely be deprecated in the future.
output_tooltips: The selected case value, or the default when the index is out of range.

value.tooltip: The value to pass through when the flow is enabled.

select.tooltip: When True the value passes through; when False execution is blocked.

message.tooltip: Optional message shown in a dialog when the flow is blocked. Leave empty for silent operation.

Basic data handling: ContinueFlow.name: Basic data handling: ContinueFlow
Basic data handling: ContinueFlow.description:
Conditionally enable or disable a flow.

This node takes a value and either passes it through or blocks execution
based on the 'select' parameter. When 'select' is True, the value passes through;
when False, execution is blocked.

When a `message` is provided ComfyUI will display it in a dialog.
Leave it empty for silent operation.
output_tooltips: The input value, or an execution blocker when the flow is disabled.

value.tooltip: The value to route to one of the two outputs.

select.tooltip: When True the value is emitted on the 'true' output, otherwise on the 'false' output.

Basic data handling: FlowSelect.name: Basic data handling: FlowSelect
Basic data handling: FlowSelect.description:
Select the direction of the flow.

This node takes a value and directs it to either the "true" or "false" output.

Note: for dynamic switching in a Data Flow you might want to use
"filter select" instead.
output_tooltips: Receives the value when select is True (otherwise blocked).
Receives the value when select is False (otherwise blocked).

value.tooltip: Any value; passed through unchanged while forcing recalculation.

Basic data handling: ForceCalculation.name: Basic data handling: ForceCalculation
Basic data handling: ForceCalculation.description:
Forces recalculation of the connected nodes.

This node passes the input directly to the output but prevents caching
by marking itself as an output node and also indicates the out has changed.
Use this when you need to ensure nodes are always recalculated.
output_tooltips: The unchanged input value.

E/O.tooltip: Chain these sockets together to force execution order.

any node output.tooltip: Connect any output of the nodes whose execution order you want to force; it is passed through.

Basic data handling: ExecutionOrder.name: Basic data handling: ExecutionOrder
Basic data handling: ExecutionOrder.description:
Force execution order in the workflow.

This node is lightweight and does not affect the workflow. It is used to force
the execution order of nodes in the workflow. You only need to chain this node
with the other execution order nodes in the desired order and add any
output of the nodes you want to force execution order on.

This node also passes through any input connected to "any node output" as
its second output.
output_tooltips: Chain to the next execution-order node.
The 'any node output' value passed through unchanged.

input.tooltip: The input to test whether it is connected.

Basic data handling: IsConnected.name: Basic data handling: IsConnected
Basic data handling: IsConnected.description:
Checks if the input is connected.

This node returns True if the 'input' is connected to another node's output,
and False otherwise.
output_tooltips: True when the input is connected to another node's output, otherwise False.

item_0.tooltip: One of the items of the Data List. Connect more values to add more items.

Basic data handling: DataListCreate.name: Basic data handling: DataListCreate
Basic data handling: DataListCreate.description:
Creates a new Data List from items.

This node creates and returns a Data List. The list of items is dynamically
extended based on the number of inputs provided.
output_tooltips: The items as a ComfyUI data list.

item_0.tooltip: One of the items of the Data List; each may itself be a list, producing a list of lists.

Basic data handling: DataListListCreate.name: Basic data handling: DataListListCreate
Basic data handling: DataListListCreate.description:
Creates a new Data List from items.

This node creates and returns a Data List. The list of items is dynamically
extended based on the number of inputs provided.

Each input can be a list, so you'll get a list of lists.
output_tooltips: The items as a ComfyUI data list of lists.

item_0.tooltip: One of the boolean items of the Data List. Connect more values to add more items.

Basic data handling: DataListCreateFromB.name: Basic data handling: DataListCreateFromBoolean
Basic data handling: DataListCreateFromB.description:
Creates a new Data List from BOOLEAN items.

This node creates and returns a Data List. The list of items is dynamically
extended based on the number of inputs provided.
output_tooltips: The boolean items as a ComfyUI data list.

item_0.tooltip: One of the float items of the Data List. Connect more values to add more items.

Basic data handling: DataListCreateFromF.name: Basic data handling: DataListCreateFromFloat
Basic data handling: DataListCreateFromF.description:
Creates a new Data List from FLOAT items.

This node creates and returns a Data List. The list of items is dynamically
extended based on the number of inputs provided.
output_tooltips: The float items as a ComfyUI data list.

item_0.tooltip: One of the integer items of the Data List. Connect more values to add more items.

Basic data handling: DataListCreateFromI.name: Basic data handling: DataListCreateFromInt
Basic data handling: DataListCreateFromI.description:
Creates a new Data List from INT items.

This node creates and returns a Data List. The list of items is dynamically
extended based on the number of inputs provided.
output_tooltips: The integer items as a ComfyUI data list.

item_0.tooltip: One of the string items of the Data List. Connect more values to add more items.

Basic data handling: DataListCreateFromS.name: Basic data handling: DataListCreateFromString
Basic data handling: DataListCreateFromS.description:
Creates a new Data List from STRING items.

This node creates and returns a Data List. The list of items is dynamically
extended based on the number of inputs provided.
output_tooltips: The string items as a ComfyUI data list.

Basic data handling: DataListAll.name: Basic data handling: DataListAll
Basic data handling: DataListAll.description:
Check if all elements in the data list are true.
Returns true if all elements are true (or if the list is empty).
output_tooltips: True when every element is truthy (or the list is empty).

Basic data handling: DataListAny.name: Basic data handling: DataListAny
Basic data handling: DataListAny.description:
Check if any element in the data list is true.
Returns true if at least one element is true. Returns false if the list is empty.
output_tooltips: True when at least one element is truthy (False for an empty list).

list.tooltip: The Data List to append to.

item.tooltip: The item to append at the end.

Basic data handling: DataListAppend.name: Basic data handling: DataListAppend
Basic data handling: DataListAppend.description:
Adds an item to the end of a list.

This node takes a list and any item as inputs, then returns the modified
list with the new item appended.
output_tooltips: A new Data List with the item appended.

value.tooltip: The value to look for.

Basic data handling: DataListContains.name: Basic data handling: DataListContains
Basic data handling: DataListContains.description:
Checks if a list contains a specified value.

This node takes a list and a value as inputs, then returns True if the value
is present in the list, and False otherwise.
output_tooltips: True when the value is present in the list.

list.tooltip: The Data List to count in.

value.tooltip: The value whose occurrences are counted.

Basic data handling: DataListCount.name: Basic data handling: DataListCount
Basic data handling: DataListCount.description:
Counts the number of occurrences of a value in a list.

This node takes a list and a value as inputs, then returns the number of times
the value appears in the list.
output_tooltips: The number of times the value occurs in the list.

start.tooltip: Index assigned to the first element.

Basic data handling: DataListEnumerate.name: Basic data handling: DataListEnumerate
Basic data handling: DataListEnumerate.description:
Enumerate a data list, returning a list of [index, value] pairs.
Optionally, specify a starting value for the index.
output_tooltips: A Data List of [index, value] pairs.

list_b.tooltip: Second Data List whose elements are appended.

Basic data handling: DataListExtend.name: Basic data handling: DataListExtend
Basic data handling: DataListExtend.description:
Extends a list by appending elements from another list.

This node takes two lists as input and returns a new list that contains
all elements from both lists.
output_tooltips: A new Data List with all elements of both inputs.

value.tooltip: The Data List of values to filter.

filter.tooltip: Data List of booleans; items whose filter is False are kept.

Basic data handling: DataListFilter.name: Basic data handling: DataListFilter
Basic data handling: DataListFilter.description:
Filters a Data List using boolean values.

This node takes a value Data List and a filter Data List (containing only boolean values).
It returns a new Data List containing only the elements from the value list where the
corresponding element in the filter list is False.

If the lists have different lengths, the last element of the shorter list is repeated
till the lengths are matching.
output_tooltips: The values kept where the filter was False.

value.tooltip: The Data List of values to split.

select.tooltip: Data List of booleans routing each value to the 'true' or 'false' output.

Basic data handling: DataListFilterSelec.name: Basic data handling: DataListFilterSelect
Basic data handling: DataListFilterSelec.description:
Filters a Data List using boolean values.

This node takes a value Data List and a filter Data List (containing only boolean values).
It returns two new Data Lists containing only the elements from the value list where the
corresponding element in the filter list is true or false.

If the lists have different lengths, the last element of the shorter list is repeated
till the lengths are matching.
output_tooltips: Values whose selector was True.
Values whose selector was False.

list.tooltip: The Data List to read from.

Basic data handling: DataListFirst.name: Basic data handling: DataListFirst
Basic data handling: DataListFirst.description:
Returns the first element in a list.

This node takes a list as input and returns the first element of the list.
If the list is empty, it returns None.
output_tooltips: The first element of the list (None when empty).

list.tooltip: The Data List to read from.

index.tooltip: Position of the item; negative counts from the end.

Basic data handling: DataListGetItem.name: Basic data handling: DataListGetItem
Basic data handling: DataListGetItem.description:
Retrieves an item at a specified position in a list.

This node takes a list and an index as inputs, then returns the item at the specified index.
Negative indices count from the end of the list.
Out of range indices return None.
output_tooltips: The item at the index (None when out of range).

value.tooltip: The value whose first occurrence is located.

start.tooltip: Start position of the search slice.

end.tooltip: End position of the search slice (-1 means the end).

Basic data handling: DataListIndex.name: Basic data handling: DataListIndex
Basic data handling: DataListIndex.description:
Returns the index of the first occurrence of a value in a list.

This node takes a list and a value as inputs, then returns the index of the first
occurrence of the value. Optional start and end parameters limit the search to a slice
of the list. Returns -1 if the value is not present.
output_tooltips: Index of the first occurrence (-1 when the value is absent).

list.tooltip: The Data List to insert into.

index.tooltip: Position at which to insert the item.

Basic data handling: DataListInsert.name: Basic data handling: DataListInsert
Basic data handling: DataListInsert.description:
Inserts an item at a specified position in a list.

This node takes a list, an index, and any item as inputs, then returns a new
list with the item inserted at the specified index.
output_tooltips: A new Data List with the item inserted at the index.

list.tooltip: The Data List to read from.

Basic data handling: DataListLast.name: Basic data handling: DataListLast
Basic data handling: DataListLast.description:
Returns the last element in a list.

This node takes a list as input and returns the last element of the list.
If the list is empty, it returns None.
output_tooltips: The last element of the list (None when empty).

Basic data handling: DataListLength.name: Basic data handling: DataListLength
Basic data handling: DataListLength.description:
Counts the number of items in a list.

This node takes a list as input and returns its length as an integer.
output_tooltips: The number of items in the list.

Basic data handling: DataListMax.name: Basic data handling: DataListMax
Basic data handling: DataListMax.description:
Finds the maximum value in a list of numbers.

This node takes a list of numbers (either FLOAT or INT) and returns
the maximum value. Returns None if the list is empty or if it contains
non-numeric values.
output_tooltips: The maximum value (None when empty or not comparable).

Basic data handling: DataListMin.name: Basic data handling: DataListMin
Basic data handling: DataListMin.description:
Finds the minimum value in a list of numbers.

This node takes a list of numbers (either FLOAT or INT) and returns
the minimum value. Returns None if the list is empty or if it contains
non-numeric values.
output_tooltips: The minimum value (None when empty or not comparable).

list.tooltip: The Data List to pop from.

index.tooltip: Position of the item to remove (-1 = last item).

Basic data handling: DataListPop.name: Basic data handling: DataListPop
Basic data handling: DataListPop.description:
Removes and returns an item at a specified position in a list.

This node takes a list and an index as inputs, then returns both the new list
with the item removed and the removed item. If no index is specified,
removes and returns the last item.
When the list is empty, the item is None.
output_tooltips: The list with the item removed.
The removed item (None when empty or the index is invalid).

list.tooltip: The Data List to pop a random element from.

seed.tooltip: Seed for reproducible selection. Leave empty to pick randomly each run.

Basic data handling: DataListPopRandom.name: Basic data handling: DataListPopRandom
Basic data handling: DataListPopRandom.description:
Removes and returns a random element from a list.

This node takes a list as input and returns the list with the random element removed
and the removed element itself. If the list is empty, it returns None for the element.
An optional seed can be provided for reproducible selection.
output_tooltips: The list with a random element removed.
The removed element (None when the list is empty).

start.tooltip: First number of the sequence (inclusive).

step.tooltip: Step between numbers; must not be 0.

Basic data handling: DataListRange.name: Basic data handling: DataListRange
Basic data handling: DataListRange.description:
Creates a data list containing a sequence of numbers.

This node generates a sequence of numbers similar to Python's range() function.
It takes start, stop, and step parameters to define the sequence.
output_tooltips: The generated numbers as a Data List.

list.tooltip: The Data List to remove from.

value.tooltip: The value whose first occurrence is removed.

Basic data handling: DataListRemove.name: Basic data handling: DataListRemove
Basic data handling: DataListRemove.description:
Removes the first occurrence of a specified value from a list.

This node takes a list and a value as inputs, then returns a new list with
the first occurrence of the value removed. Raises a ValueError if the value is not present.
output_tooltips: The list with the first occurrence removed.
True when the value was present and removed.

Basic data handling: DataListReverse.name: Basic data handling: DataListReverse
Basic data handling: DataListReverse.description:
Reverses the order of items in a list.

This node takes a list as input and returns a new list with the items in reversed order.
output_tooltips: A new Data List with the items in reversed order.

index.tooltip: Position of the item to replace.

value.tooltip: The new value.

Basic data handling: DataListSetItem.name: Basic data handling: DataListSetItem
Basic data handling: DataListSetItem.description:
Sets an item at a specified position in a list.

This node takes a list, an index, and a value, then returns a new list with
the item at the specified index replaced by the value.
output_tooltips: A new Data List with the item at the index replaced.

seed.tooltip: Seed for reproducible shuffling.

Basic data handling: DataListShuffle.name: Basic data handling: DataListShuffle
Basic data handling: DataListShuffle.description:
Shuffles the items in a list using a seed for reproducibility.

This node takes a list and a seed as input and returns a new shuffled list.
output_tooltips: A new Data List with the items shuffled.

start.tooltip: Start index (inclusive).

stop.tooltip: Stop index (exclusive); INT_MAX means the end.

Basic data handling: DataListSlice.name: Basic data handling: DataListSlice
Basic data handling: DataListSlice.description:
Creates a slice of a list.

This node takes a list and start/stop/step parameters, and returns a new list
containing the specified slice of the original list.
output_tooltips: The requested slice of the list.

reverse.tooltip: Sort in descending order when True.

Basic data handling: DataListSort.name: Basic data handling: DataListSort
Basic data handling: DataListSort.description:
Sorts the items in a list.

This node takes a list as input and returns a new sorted list.
Options include sorting in reverse order and using a key function.
output_tooltips: A new sorted Data List.

list.tooltip: The Data List of numbers to sum.

start.tooltip: Initial value added to the sum.

Basic data handling: DataListSum.name: Basic data handling: DataListSum
Basic data handling: DataListSum.description:
Sum all elements of the data list.
Returns 0 for an empty list.
output_tooltips: The total as an integer.
The total as a float.

Basic data handling: DataListZip.name: Basic data handling: DataListZip
Basic data handling: DataListZip.description:
Combines multiple lists element-wise.

This node takes multiple Data Lists as input and returns a new Data List
where each item is a list containing the corresponding elements from the input lists.
The length of the output list will be equal to the length of the shortest input list.
output_tooltips: Elements combined element-wise; length matches the shortest input.

Basic data handling: DataListToList.name: Basic data handling: DataListToList
Basic data handling: DataListToList.description:
Converts a ComfyUI Data List into a LIST object.

This node takes a Data List input (which is typically a list of items with the same type)
and converts it to a LIST object (a Python list as a single variable).
output_tooltips: The Data List's items as a single Python LIST value.

Basic data handling: DataListToSet.name: Basic data handling: DataListToSet
Basic data handling: DataListToSet.description:
Converts a ComfyUI Data List into a LIST object.

This node takes a Data List input (which is typically a list of items with the same type)
and converts it to a LIST object (a Python list as a single variable).
output_tooltips: A SET of the Data List's unique items.

key_0.tooltip: Key for a key-value pair. Connect more keys to add more pairs.

value_0.tooltip: Value paired with the key of the same index.

Basic data handling: DictCreate.name: Basic data handling: DictCreate
Basic data handling: DictCreate.description:
Creates a new empty dictionary.

This node creates and returns a new empty dictionary object.
output_tooltips: The created DICT.

key_0.tooltip: Key for a key-value pair. Connect more keys to add more pairs.

value_0.tooltip: Boolean value paired with the key of the same index.

Basic data handling: DictCreateFromBoole.name: Basic data handling: DictCreateFromBoolean
Basic data handling: DictCreateFromBoole.description:
Creates a new empty dictionary.

This node creates and returns a new empty dictionary object.
output_tooltips: The created DICT.

key_0.tooltip: Key for a key-value pair. Connect more keys to add more pairs.

value_0.tooltip: Float value paired with the key of the same index.

Basic data handling: DictCreateFromFloat.name: Basic data handling: DictCreateFromFloat
Basic data handling: DictCreateFromFloat.description:
Creates a new empty dictionary.

This node creates and returns a new empty dictionary object.
output_tooltips: The created DICT.

key_0.tooltip: Key for a key-value pair. Connect more keys to add more pairs.

value_0.tooltip: Integer value paired with the key of the same index.

Basic data handling: DictCreateFromInt.name: Basic data handling: DictCreateFromInt
Basic data handling: DictCreateFromInt.description:
Creates a new empty dictionary.

This node creates and returns a new empty dictionary object.
output_tooltips: The created DICT.

key_0.tooltip: Key for a key-value pair. Connect more keys to add more pairs.

value_0.tooltip: String value paired with the key of the same index.

Basic data handling: DictCreateFromStrin.name: Basic data handling: DictCreateFromString
Basic data handling: DictCreateFromStrin.description:
Creates a new empty dictionary.

This node creates and returns a new empty dictionary object.
output_tooltips: The created DICT.

item.tooltip: A data list of (key, value) pairs to build the DICT from.

Basic data handling: DictCreateFromItems.name: Basic data handling: DictCreateFromItemsDataList
Basic data handling: DictCreateFromItems.description:
Creates a dictionary from a list of key-value pairs.

This node takes a list of key-value pairs (tuples) and builds a dictionary from them.
output_tooltips: The created DICT.

items.tooltip: A LIST of (key, value) pairs to build the DICT from.

Basic data handling: DictCreateFromItems.name: Basic data handling: DictCreateFromItemsList
Basic data handling: DictCreateFromItems.description:
Creates a dictionary from a list of key-value pairs.

This node takes a list of key-value pairs (tuples) and builds a dictionary from them.
output_tooltips: The created DICT.

values.tooltip: The values paired with the keys by position.

Basic data handling: DictCreateFromLists.name: Basic data handling: DictCreateFromLists
Basic data handling: DictCreateFromLists.description:
Creates a dictionary from separate lists of keys and values.

This node takes a list of keys and a list of values, then creates a dictionary
by pairing corresponding elements from each list. If the lists are of different
lengths, only pairs up to the length of the shorter list are used.
output_tooltips: The DICT created by pairing the two lists (up to the shorter length).

Basic data handling: DictCompare.name: Basic data handling: DictCompare
Basic data handling: DictCompare.description:
Compares two dictionaries and reports differences.

This node takes two dictionaries and compares them, returning information about
their equality, any keys that exist in only one dictionary, and any keys with
different values.
output_tooltips: True when the two DICTs are equal.
Keys present only in the first DICT.
Keys present only in the second DICT.
Shared keys whose values differ.

Basic data handling: DictContainsKey.name: Basic data handling: DictContainsKey
Basic data handling: DictContainsKey.description:
Checks if a key exists in a dictionary.

This node takes a dictionary and a key as inputs, then returns True if the key
exists in the dictionary, and False otherwise.
output_tooltips: True when the key exists in the DICT.

keys_to_exclude.tooltip: Keys to drop from the result.

Basic data handling: DictExcludeKeys.name: Basic data handling: DictExcludeKeys
Basic data handling: DictExcludeKeys.description:
Creates a new dictionary excluding the specified keys.

This node takes a dictionary and a list of keys, then returns a new dictionary
containing all key-value pairs except those with keys in the provided list.
output_tooltips: A new DICT without the excluded keys.

keys.tooltip: Keys to keep in the result.

Basic data handling: DictFilterByKeys.name: Basic data handling: DictFilterByKeys
Basic data handling: DictFilterByKeys.description:
Creates a new dictionary with only the specified keys.

This node takes a dictionary and a list of keys, then returns a new dictionary
containing only the key-value pairs for the keys that exist in the original dictionary.
output_tooltips: A new DICT containing only the selected keys.

keys.tooltip: The keys of the new DICT.

value.tooltip: Default value assigned to every key (None when not provided).

Basic data handling: DictFromKeys.name: Basic data handling: DictFromKeys
Basic data handling: DictFromKeys.description:
Creates a dictionary from a list of keys and a default value.

This node takes a list of keys and an optional value, then creates a new
dictionary where each key is associated with the value. If no value is
provided, None is used.
output_tooltips: A DICT mapping each key to the given value.

key.tooltip: The key whose value is retrieved.

default.tooltip: Value returned when the key is missing (None when not provided).

Basic data handling: DictGet.name: Basic data handling: DictGet
Basic data handling: DictGet.description:
Retrieves a value from a dictionary using the specified key.

This node gets the value for the specified key from a dictionary.
If the key is not found and a default value is provided, that default is returned.
Otherwise, it returns None.
output_tooltips: The value for the key, or the default when the key is absent.

Basic data handling: DictGetKeysValues.name: Basic data handling: DictGetKeysValues
Basic data handling: DictGetKeysValues.description:
Returns keys and values as separate lists.

This node takes a dictionary and returns two lists: one containing
all keys and another containing all corresponding values.
output_tooltips: All keys of the DICT.
All values of the DICT, in the same order as the keys.

keys.tooltip: The keys whose values are retrieved.

default.tooltip: Value used for keys that are missing (None when not provided).

Basic data handling: DictGetMultiple.name: Basic data handling: DictGetMultiple
Basic data handling: DictGetMultiple.description:
Retrieves multiple values from a dictionary using a list of keys.

This node takes a dictionary and a list of keys, then returns a list
containing the corresponding values. If a key is not found, the default
value is used for that position.
output_tooltips: The value for each requested key, using the default for missing keys.

input_dict.tooltip: The DICT whose keys and values are swapped.

Basic data handling: DictInvert.name: Basic data handling: DictInvert
Basic data handling: DictInvert.description:
Creates a new dictionary with keys and values swapped.

This node takes a dictionary as input and returns a new dictionary where
the keys become values and values become keys. Note that values must be
hashable to be used as keys in the new dictionary.
output_tooltips: The DICT with keys and values swapped.
True when the inversion succeeded (values were hashable).

Basic data handling: DictItems.name: Basic data handling: DictItems
Basic data handling: DictItems.description:
Returns all key-value pairs in a dictionary.

This node takes a dictionary and returns a list of tuples, where each tuple
contains a key-value pair from the dictionary.
output_tooltips: A LIST of (key, value) tuples, one per entry.

Basic data handling: DictKeys.name: Basic data handling: DictKeys
Basic data handling: DictKeys.description:
Returns all keys in a dictionary.

This node takes a dictionary and returns a list containing all of its keys.
output_tooltips: A LIST of all keys in the DICT.

Basic data handling: DictLength.name: Basic data handling: DictLength
Basic data handling: DictLength.description:
Returns the number of key-value pairs in a dictionary.

This node takes a dictionary as input and returns its length (number of items).
output_tooltips: The number of key-value pairs in the DICT.

dict2.tooltip: Optional DICT to merge; its values win over dict1.

dict3.tooltip: Optional DICT to merge; its values win over earlier ones.

dict4.tooltip: Optional DICT to merge; its values win over earlier ones.

Basic data handling: DictMerge.name: Basic data handling: DictMerge
Basic data handling: DictMerge.description:
Merges multiple dictionaries into a single dictionary.

This node takes multiple dictionaries as input and combines them into a single
dictionary. If there are duplicate keys, values from later dictionaries take precedence.
output_tooltips: The merged DICT; later inputs take precedence on duplicate keys.

key.tooltip: The key whose entry is removed.

default_value.tooltip: Value returned when the key is absent (None when not provided).

Basic data handling: DictPop.name: Basic data handling: DictPop
Basic data handling: DictPop.description:
Removes and returns a key-value pair from a dictionary.

This node takes a dictionary and a key as inputs, removes the specified key
from the dictionary, and returns both the modified dictionary and the value
associated with the key. If the key is not found and a default value is provided,
that default is returned. Otherwise, an error is raised.
output_tooltips: The DICT with the key removed.
The removed value (or the default when the key was absent).

input_dict.tooltip: The DICT to pop an entry from.

Basic data handling: DictPopItem.name: Basic data handling: DictPopItem
Basic data handling: DictPopItem.description:
Removes and returns an arbitrary key-value pair from a dictionary.

This node takes a dictionary as input, removes an arbitrary key-value pair,
and returns the modified dictionary along with the removed key and value.
If operation fails, no error is thrown, but the last argument is `False`,
and the dictionary is returned intact.
output_tooltips: The DICT with one entry removed.
The removed key.
The removed value.
False when the DICT was empty or the operation failed.

input_dict.tooltip: The DICT to pop a random entry from.

seed.tooltip: Seed for reproducible selection. Leave empty to pick randomly each run.

Basic data handling: DictPopRandom.name: Basic data handling: DictPopRandom
Basic data handling: DictPopRandom.description:
Removes and returns a random key-value pair from a dictionary.

This node takes a dictionary as input, removes a random key-value pair,
and returns the modified dictionary along with the removed key and value.
If the dictionary is empty, it returns empty values.
An optional seed can be provided for reproducible selection.
output_tooltips: The DICT with a random entry removed.
The removed key.
The removed value.
False when the DICT was empty or the operation failed.

Basic data handling: DictRemove.name: Basic data handling: DictRemove
Basic data handling: DictRemove.description:
Removes a key-value pair from a dictionary.

This node takes a dictionary and a key as inputs, then returns a new
dictionary with the specified key removed. If the key doesn't exist,
the dictionary remains unchanged.
output_tooltips: The DICT with the key removed (unchanged when it was absent).
True when the key existed and was removed.

key.tooltip: The key to add or update.

value.tooltip: The value to store under the key.

Basic data handling: DictSet.name: Basic data handling: DictSet
Basic data handling: DictSet.description:
Adds or updates a key-value pair in a dictionary.

This node takes a dictionary, key, and value as inputs, then returns
a modified dictionary with the new key-value pair.
output_tooltips: A new DICT with the key set to the given value.

input_dict.tooltip: The DICT to read or modify.

default_value.tooltip: Value inserted and returned when the key is missing.

Basic data handling: DictSetDefault.name: Basic data handling: DictSetDefault
Basic data handling: DictSetDefault.description:
Returns the value for a key, setting a default if the key doesn't exist.

This node takes a dictionary, a key, and a default value. If the key exists
in the dictionary, the corresponding value is returned. If the key doesn't
exist, the default value is inserted for the key and returned.
output_tooltips: The DICT, with the default inserted when the key was missing.
The value for the key (existing or the inserted default).

dict2.tooltip: DICT whose entries are added; it wins on duplicate keys.

Basic data handling: DictUpdate.name: Basic data handling: DictUpdate
Basic data handling: DictUpdate.description:
Updates a dictionary with key-value pairs from another dictionary.

This node takes two dictionaries as inputs and returns a new dictionary that
contains all key-value pairs from both dictionaries. If there are duplicate
keys, the values from the second dictionary take precedence.
output_tooltips: The merged DICT with dict2's entries applied to dict1.

Basic data handling: DictValues.name: Basic data handling: DictValues
Basic data handling: DictValues.description:
Returns all values in a dictionary.

This node takes a dictionary and returns a list containing all of its values.
output_tooltips: A LIST of all values in the DICT.

value.tooltip: Textual form of the number to parse, e.g. "3.14". Must be a valid float.

Basic data handling: FloatCreate.name: Basic data handling: FloatCreate
Basic data handling: FloatCreate.description:
Create a FLOAT from a STRING widget.

The input string must be a valid floating-point number and will be
directly converted to a FLOAT without any further processing.
output_tooltips: The parsed FLOAT value.

Basic data handling: FloatAdd.name: Basic data handling: FloatAdd
Basic data handling: FloatAdd.description:
Adds two floating-point numbers.

This node takes two floats as input and returns their sum.
output_tooltips: The sum of the two floats.

Basic data handling: FloatSubtract.name: Basic data handling: FloatSubtract
Basic data handling: FloatSubtract.description:
Subtracts one floating-point number from another.

This node takes two floats as input and returns the result of subtracting
the second float from the first.
output_tooltips: The difference float1 - float2.

Basic data handling: FloatMultiply.name: Basic data handling: FloatMultiply
Basic data handling: FloatMultiply.description:
Multiplies two floating-point numbers.

This node takes two floats as input and returns their product.
output_tooltips: The product of the two floats.

Basic data handling: FloatDivide.name: Basic data handling: FloatDivide
Basic data handling: FloatDivide.description:
Divides one floating-point number by another.

This node takes two floats as input and returns the result of division.
It raises a ValueError if the divisor is 0.
output_tooltips: The quotient float1 / float2.

float2.tooltip: Divisor; a value of 0 yields +/-infinity instead of an error.

Basic data handling: FloatDivideSafe.name: Basic data handling: FloatDivideSafe
Basic data handling: FloatDivideSafe.description:
Divides one floating-point number by another.

This node takes two floats as input and returns the result of the division.
It returns positive or negative infinity if the divisor is 0 (assumed to be +0.0).
output_tooltips: The quotient float1 / float2, or +/-infinity (NaN for 0/0) when the divisor is 0.

float_value.tooltip: The float to decompose into an exact integer ratio.

Basic data handling: FloatAsIntegerRatio.name: Basic data handling: FloatAsIntegerRatio
Basic data handling: FloatAsIntegerRatio.description:
Returns the integer ratio of a floating-point number.

This node takes a floating-point number and returns two integers,
which represent the ratio as numerator and denominator.
output_tooltips: Numerator of the exact ratio.
Denominator of the exact ratio.

hex_value.tooltip: Hexadecimal float string as produced by the "to hex" node, e.g. 0x1.8p+1.

Basic data handling: FloatFromHex.name: Basic data handling: FloatFromHex
Basic data handling: FloatFromHex.description:
Converts a hexadecimal string to its corresponding floating-point number.

This node takes a hexadecimal float string as input and returns the float.
output_tooltips: The decoded FLOAT value.

float_value.tooltip: The float to format as a hexadecimal string.

Basic data handling: FloatHex.name: Basic data handling: FloatHex
Basic data handling: FloatHex.description:
Converts a floating-point number to its hexadecimal representation.

This node takes a float as input and returns its hexadecimal string representation.
output_tooltips: Hexadecimal representation of the float, e.g. '0x1.0000000000000p+0'.

Basic data handling: FloatIsInteger.name: Basic data handling: FloatIsInteger
Basic data handling: FloatIsInteger.description:
Checks if a floating-point number is an integer.

This node takes a floating-point number as input and returns True if the number
is an integer, otherwise False.
output_tooltips: True when the float has no fractional part (e.g. 3.0), otherwise False.

exponent.tooltip: The exponent to raise the base to.

Basic data handling: FloatPower.name: Basic data handling: FloatPower
Basic data handling: FloatPower.description:
Raises one floating-point number to the power of another.

This node takes two floats as input and returns the result of raising
the first float to the power of the second.
output_tooltips: The result of base ** exponent.

decimal_places.tooltip: Number of decimal places to keep (0 rounds to a whole number).

Basic data handling: FloatRound.name: Basic data handling: FloatRound
Basic data handling: FloatRound.description:
Rounds a floating-point number to the specified number of decimal places.

This node takes a float and an integer for decimal places as inputs,
and returns the rounded result.
output_tooltips: The float rounded to the requested number of decimal places.

value.tooltip: Textual form of the integer to parse. Prefixes 0b/0o/0x select binary/octal/hexadecimal.

Basic data handling: IntCreate.name: Basic data handling: IntCreate
Basic data handling: IntCreate.description:
Create an INT from a STRING widget.

The input string must be a valid integer number and will be
directly converted to an INT without any further processing.

Strings starting with "0b" are interpreted as binary numbers,
"0o" as octal numbers, and "0x" as hexadecimal numbers.

Note: This doesn't handle ones' complement as the data size is unknown.
output_tooltips: The parsed INT value.

value.tooltip: Textual form of the integer as written in the chosen base.

base.tooltip: Numeric base to interpret the string in (>= 2), e.g. 2, 8, 10 or 16.

Basic data handling: IntCreateWithBase.name: Basic data handling: IntCreateWithBase
Basic data handling: IntCreateWithBase.description:
Create an INT from a STRING with a given base.

The input string must be a valid integer number and will be
directly converted to an INT without any further processing.
output_tooltips: The parsed INT value.

Basic data handling: IntAdd.name: Basic data handling: IntAdd
Basic data handling: IntAdd.description:
Adds two integers.

This node takes two integers as input and returns their sum.
output_tooltips: The sum of the two integers.

Basic data handling: IntSubtract.name: Basic data handling: IntSubtract
Basic data handling: IntSubtract.description:
Subtracts one integer from another.

This node takes two integers as input and returns the result of subtracting
the second integer from the first.
output_tooltips: The difference int1 - int2.

Basic data handling: IntMultiply.name: Basic data handling: IntMultiply
Basic data handling: IntMultiply.description:
Multiplies two integers.

This node takes two integers as input and returns their product.
output_tooltips: The product of the two integers.

Basic data handling: IntDivide.name: Basic data handling: IntDivide
Basic data handling: IntDivide.description:
Divides one integer by another.

This node takes two integers as input and returns the result of integer
division. It raises a ValueError if the divisor is 0.
output_tooltips: The integer quotient int1 // int2 (fractional part discarded).

int2.tooltip: Divisor; a value of 0 returns the infinity sentinel instead of an error.

infinity.tooltip: Value returned as +infinity when dividing by zero (negated for negative results).

Basic data handling: IntDivideSafe.name: Basic data handling: IntDivideSafe
Basic data handling: IntDivideSafe.description:
Divides one integer by another.

This node takes two integers as input and returns the result of the integer
division. It returns the positive or negative infinity value if the divisor is 0.
output_tooltips: The integer quotient int1 // int2, or the +/-infinity sentinel when the divisor is 0.

Basic data handling: IntBitCount.name: Basic data handling: IntBitCount
Basic data handling: IntBitCount.description:
Returns the number of 1 bits in the binary representation of an integer.

This node takes an integer as input and returns the count of set bits.
output_tooltips: Number of 1 bits in the binary (two's complement) representation.

Basic data handling: IntBitLength.name: Basic data handling: IntBitLength
Basic data handling: IntBitLength.description:
Returns the number of bits required to represent an integer in binary.

This node takes an integer as input and returns the number of bits needed
to represent it, excluding the sign and leading zeros.
output_tooltips: Number of bits required to represent the value (excluding the sign and leading zeros).

bytes_value.tooltip: The bytes object to decode into an integer.

byteorder.tooltip: Byte order: 'big' (most significant byte first) or 'little'.

signed.tooltip: When True the bytes are read as a two's complement signed integer.

Basic data handling: IntFromBytes.name: Basic data handling: IntFromBytes
Basic data handling: IntFromBytes.description:
Converts a bytes object to an integer.

This class method takes bytes, byte order, and signed flag as inputs and
returns an integer.
output_tooltips: The decoded INT value.

Basic data handling: IntModulus.name: Basic data handling: IntModulus
Basic data handling: IntModulus.description:
Returns the modulus of two integers.

This node takes two integers as input and returns the remainder when the
first integer is divided by the second.
output_tooltips: The remainder of int1 divided by int2 (same sign as the divisor).

exponent.tooltip: The exponent to raise the base to.

Basic data handling: IntPower.name: Basic data handling: IntPower
Basic data handling: IntPower.description:
Raises one integer to the power of another.

This node takes two integers as input and returns the result of raising
the first integer to the power of the second.
output_tooltips: The result of base ** exponent.

length.tooltip: Number of bytes in the result (must be large enough to hold the value).

byteorder.tooltip: Byte order of the output: 'big' (most significant byte first) or 'little'.

signed.tooltip: When True the value is encoded as a two's complement signed integer.

Basic data handling: IntToBytes.name: Basic data handling: IntToBytes
Basic data handling: IntToBytes.description:
Converts an integer to its byte representation.

This node takes an integer, byte length, and byte order as inputs and
returns the bytes object representation of the integer.
output_tooltips: The bytes object representation of the integer.

item_0.tooltip: One of the items of the LIST. Connect more values to add more items.

Basic data handling: ListCreate.name: Basic data handling: ListCreate
Basic data handling: ListCreate.description:
Creates a new LIST from items.

This node creates and returns a LIST. The list of items is dynamically
extended based on the number of inputs provided.
output_tooltips: The LIST containing the provided items.

item_0.tooltip: One of the boolean items of the LIST. Connect more values to add more items.

Basic data handling: ListCreateFromBoole.name: Basic data handling: ListCreateFromBoolean
Basic data handling: ListCreateFromBoole.description:
Creates a new LIST from BOOLEAN items.

This node creates and returns a LIST. The list of items is dynamically
extended based on the number of inputs provided.
output_tooltips: The LIST containing the provided boolean items.

item_0.tooltip: One of the float items of the LIST. Connect more values to add more items.

Basic data handling: ListCreateFromFloat.name: Basic data handling: ListCreateFromFloat
Basic data handling: ListCreateFromFloat.description:
Creates a new LIST from FLOAT items.

This node creates and returns a LIST. The list of items is dynamically
extended based on the number of inputs provided.
output_tooltips: The LIST containing the provided float items.

item_0.tooltip: One of the integer items of the LIST. Connect more values to add more items.

Basic data handling: ListCreateFromInt.name: Basic data handling: ListCreateFromInt
Basic data handling: ListCreateFromInt.description:
Creates a new LIST from INT items.

This node creates and returns a LIST. The list of items is dynamically
extended based on the number of inputs provided.
output_tooltips: The LIST containing the provided integer items.

item_0.tooltip: One of the string items of the LIST. Connect more values to add more items.

Basic data handling: ListCreateFromStrin.name: Basic data handling: ListCreateFromString
Basic data handling: ListCreateFromStrin.description:
Creates a new LIST from STRING items.

This node creates and returns a LIST. The list of items is dynamically
extended based on the number of inputs provided.
output_tooltips: The LIST containing the provided string items.

Basic data handling: ListAll.name: Basic data handling: ListAll
Basic data handling: ListAll.description:
Check if all elements in the list are true.
Returns true if all elements are true (or if the list is empty).
output_tooltips: True when every element is truthy (or the LIST is empty).

Basic data handling: ListAny.name: Basic data handling: ListAny
Basic data handling: ListAny.description:
Check if any element in the list is true.
Returns true if at least one element is true. Returns false if the list is empty.
output_tooltips: True when at least one element is truthy (False for an empty LIST).

item.tooltip: The item to append at the end.

Basic data handling: ListAppend.name: Basic data handling: ListAppend
Basic data handling: ListAppend.description:
Adds an item to the end of a LIST.

This node takes a LIST and any item as inputs, then returns a new LIST
with the item appended to the end.
output_tooltips: A new LIST with the item appended.

value.tooltip: The value to look for.

Basic data handling: ListContains.name: Basic data handling: ListContains
Basic data handling: ListContains.description:
Checks if a LIST contains a specified value.

This node takes a LIST and a value as inputs, then returns True if the value
is present in the LIST, and False otherwise.
output_tooltips: True when the value is present in the LIST.

value.tooltip: The value whose occurrences are counted.

Basic data handling: ListCount.name: Basic data handling: ListCount
Basic data handling: ListCount.description:
Counts the number of occurrences of a value in a LIST.

This node takes a LIST and a value as inputs, then returns the number of times
the value appears in the LIST.
output_tooltips: The number of times the value occurs in the LIST.

start.tooltip: Index assigned to the first element.

Basic data handling: ListEnumerate.name: Basic data handling: ListEnumerate
Basic data handling: ListEnumerate.description:
Enumerate a list, returning a list of [index, value] pairs.
Optionally, specify a starting value for the index.
output_tooltips: A LIST of [index, value] pairs.

list2.tooltip: Second LIST whose elements are appended.

Basic data handling: ListExtend.name: Basic data handling: ListExtend
Basic data handling: ListExtend.description:
Extends a LIST by appending elements from another LIST.

This node takes two LIST objects as input and returns a new LIST that contains
all elements from both lists.
output_tooltips: A new LIST with all elements of both lists.

Basic data handling: ListFirst.name: Basic data handling: ListFirst
Basic data handling: ListFirst.description:
Returns the first element in a LIST.

This node takes a LIST as input and returns the first element of the list.
If the LIST is empty, it returns None.
output_tooltips: The first element of the LIST (None when empty).

index.tooltip: Position of the item; negative counts from the end.

Basic data handling: ListGetItem.name: Basic data handling: ListGetItem
Basic data handling: ListGetItem.description:
Retrieves an item at a specified position in a LIST.

This node takes a LIST and an index as inputs, then returns the item at the specified index.
Negative indices count from the end of the LIST.
Out of range indices return None.
output_tooltips: The item at the index (None when out of range).

value.tooltip: The value whose first occurrence is located.

start.tooltip: Start position of the search slice.

end.tooltip: End position of the search slice (-1 means the end of the LIST).

Basic data handling: ListIndex.name: Basic data handling: ListIndex
Basic data handling: ListIndex.description:
Returns the index of the first occurrence of a value in a LIST.

This node takes a LIST and a value as inputs, then returns the index of the first
occurrence of the value. Optional start and end parameters limit the search to a slice
of the LIST. Returns -1 if the value is not present.
output_tooltips: Index of the first occurrence (-1 when the value is absent).

index.tooltip: Position at which to insert the item.

Basic data handling: ListInsert.name: Basic data handling: ListInsert
Basic data handling: ListInsert.description:
Inserts an item at a specified position in a LIST.

This node takes a LIST, an index, and any item as inputs, then returns a new
LIST with the item inserted at the specified index.
output_tooltips: A new LIST with the item inserted at the index.

Basic data handling: ListLast.name: Basic data handling: ListLast
Basic data handling: ListLast.description:
Returns the last element in a LIST.

This node takes a LIST as input and returns the last element of the list.
If the LIST is empty, it returns None.
output_tooltips: The last element of the LIST (None when empty).

Basic data handling: ListLength.name: Basic data handling: ListLength
Basic data handling: ListLength.description:
Returns the number of items in a LIST.

This node takes a LIST as input and returns its length as an integer.
output_tooltips: The number of items in the LIST.

Basic data handling: ListMax.name: Basic data handling: ListMax
Basic data handling: ListMax.description:
Returns the maximum value in a LIST.

This node takes a LIST of comparable items and returns the maximum value.
Returns None if the LIST is empty or if items are not comparable.
output_tooltips: The maximum value (None for an empty or non-comparable LIST).

Basic data handling: ListMin.name: Basic data handling: ListMin
Basic data handling: ListMin.description:
Returns the minimum value in a LIST.

This node takes a LIST of comparable items and returns the minimum value.
Returns None if the LIST is empty or if items are not comparable.
output_tooltips: The minimum value (None for an empty or non-comparable LIST).

index.tooltip: Position of the item to remove (-1 = last item).

Basic data handling: ListPop.name: Basic data handling: ListPop
Basic data handling: ListPop.description:
Removes and returns an item at a specified position in a LIST.

This node takes a LIST and an index as inputs, then returns both the new LIST
with the item removed and the removed item. If no index is specified,
removes and returns the last item.
When the LIST is empty, the item is None.
output_tooltips: The LIST with the item removed.
The removed item (None when the LIST is empty or the index is invalid).

list.tooltip: The LIST to pop a random element from.

seed.tooltip: Seed for reproducible selection. Leave empty to pick randomly each run.

Basic data handling: ListPopRandom.name: Basic data handling: ListPopRandom
Basic data handling: ListPopRandom.description:
Removes and returns a random element from a LIST.

This node takes a LIST as input and returns the LIST with the random element removed
and the removed element itself. If the LIST is empty, it returns None for the element.
An optional seed can be provided for reproducible selection.
output_tooltips: The LIST with a random element removed.
The removed element (None when the LIST is empty).

start.tooltip: First number of the sequence (inclusive).

step.tooltip: Step between numbers; must not be 0.

Basic data handling: ListRange.name: Basic data handling: ListRange
Basic data handling: ListRange.description:
Creates a LIST containing a sequence of numbers.

This node generates a LIST of numbers similar to Python's range() function.
It takes start, stop, and step parameters to define the sequence.
output_tooltips: The generated LIST of numbers.

value.tooltip: The value whose first occurrence is removed.

Basic data handling: ListRemove.name: Basic data handling: ListRemove
Basic data handling: ListRemove.description:
Removes the first occurrence of a specified value from a LIST.

This node takes a LIST and a value as inputs, then returns a new LIST with
the first occurrence of the value removed and a success indicator. If the value
is not present, the original LIST is returned with success set to False.
output_tooltips: The LIST with the first occurrence removed.
True when the value was present and removed.

Basic data handling: ListReverse.name: Basic data handling: ListReverse
Basic data handling: ListReverse.description:
Reverses the order of items in a LIST.

This node takes a LIST as input and returns a new LIST with the items in reversed order.
output_tooltips: A new LIST with the items in reversed order.

index.tooltip: Position of the item to replace.

value.tooltip: The new value.

Basic data handling: ListSetItem.name: Basic data handling: ListSetItem
Basic data handling: ListSetItem.description:
Sets an item at a specified position in a LIST.

This node takes a LIST, an index, and a value, then returns a new LIST with
the item at the specified index replaced by the value.
output_tooltips: A new LIST with the item at the index replaced.

seed.tooltip: Seed for reproducible shuffling.

Basic data handling: ListShuffle.name: Basic data handling: ListShuffle
