Basic data handling: ListShuffle.description:
Shuffles the items in a list using a seed for reproducibility.

This node takes a LIST and a seed as input and returns a new shuffled LIST.
output_tooltips: A new LIST with the items shuffled.

start.tooltip: Start index (inclusive).

stop.tooltip: Stop index (exclusive); INT_MAX means the end.

Basic data handling: ListSlice.name: Basic data handling: ListSlice
Basic data handling: ListSlice.description:
Creates a slice of a LIST.

This node takes a LIST and start/stop/step parameters, and returns a new LIST
containing the specified slice of the original LIST.
output_tooltips: The requested slice of the LIST.

reverse.tooltip: Sort in descending order when True.

Basic data handling: ListSort.name: Basic data handling: ListSort
Basic data handling: ListSort.description:
Sorts the items in a LIST.

This node takes a LIST as input and returns a new sorted LIST.
Option includes sorting in reverse order.
output_tooltips: A new sorted LIST (the original is returned when items are not comparable).

list.tooltip: The LIST of numbers to sum.

start.tooltip: Initial value added to the sum.

Basic data handling: ListSum.name: Basic data handling: ListSum
Basic data handling: ListSum.description:
Sum all elements of the list.
Returns 0 for an empty list.
output_tooltips: The total as an integer.
The total as a float.

Basic data handling: ListToDataList.name: Basic data handling: ListToDataList
Basic data handling: ListToDataList.description:
Converts a LIST object into a ComfyUI data list.

This node takes a LIST object (Python list as a single variable) and
converts it to a ComfyUI data list, allowing its items to be processed
individually by nodes that accept data lists.
output_tooltips: The LIST's items as a ComfyUI data list.

Basic data handling: ListToSet.name: Basic data handling: ListToSet
Basic data handling: ListToSet.description:
Converts a LIST into a SET.

This node takes a LIST input and creates a new SET containing all unique elements
from the LIST, removing any duplicates.
output_tooltips: A SET of the LIST's unique items.

path.tooltip: Path to resolve to an absolute path.

Basic data handling: PathAbspath.name: Basic data handling: PathAbspath
Basic data handling: PathAbspath.description:
Returns the absolute path of a file or directory.

This node takes a path and returns its absolute (full) path
by resolving any relative path components and symbolic links.
output_tooltips: The absolute path with relative components and symlinks resolved.

path.tooltip: Path whose final filename component is returned.

Basic data handling: PathBasename.name: Basic data handling: PathBasename
Basic data handling: PathBasename.description:
Returns the base name of a path.

This node extracts the filename component from a path,
removing any directory information.
output_tooltips: The final filename component of the path.

Basic data handling: PathCommonPrefix.name: Basic data handling: PathCommonPrefix
Basic data handling: PathCommonPrefix.description:
Finds the common prefix of multiple paths.

This node returns the longest common leading component of the given paths.
output_tooltips: The longest common leading component of the given paths.

path.tooltip: Path whose directory component is returned.

Basic data handling: PathDirname.name: Basic data handling: PathDirname
Basic data handling: PathDirname.description:
Returns the directory name of a path.

This node extracts the directory component from a path,
removing the filename.
output_tooltips: The directory (parent) component of the path.

path.tooltip: Path to check for existence.

Basic data handling: PathExists.name: Basic data handling: PathExists
Basic data handling: PathExists.description:
Checks if a path exists in the filesystem.

This node returns True if the path exists (either as a file or a directory),
and False otherwise.
output_tooltips: True when the path exists as a file or directory.

path.tooltip: Path that may contain environment variables (e.g. $HOME, %USERPROFILE%).

Basic data handling: PathExpandVars.name: Basic data handling: PathExpandVars
Basic data handling: PathExpandVars.description:
Expands environment variables in a path.

This node replaces environment variables in a path with their values.
For example, $HOME or ${HOME} on Unix, or %USERPROFILE% on Windows.
output_tooltips: The path with environment variables expanded.

Basic data handling: PathGetCwd.name: Basic data handling: PathGetCwd
Basic data handling: PathGetCwd.description:
Returns the current working directory.

This node returns the current working directory as an absolute path.
output_tooltips: The current working directory as an absolute path.

path.tooltip: Path whose file extension is extracted.

Basic data handling: PathGetExtension.name: Basic data handling: PathGetExtension
Basic data handling: PathGetExtension.description:
Returns the extension of a file.

This node extracts the file extension from a path,
including the dot (e.g., '.txt').
output_tooltips: The extension including the dot (e.g. '.txt'); empty when there is none.

path.tooltip: Path whose extension is replaced.

extension.tooltip: The new extension; a leading dot is added if missing.

Basic data handling: PathSetExtension.name: Basic data handling: PathSetExtension
Basic data handling: PathSetExtension.description:
Sets the file extension for a path.

This node replaces the current extension in a path with a new one.
The extension should include the dot (e.g., '.jpg').
output_tooltips: The path with its extension replaced.

path.tooltip: File whose size in bytes is returned.

Basic data handling: PathGetSize.name: Basic data handling: PathGetSize
Basic data handling: PathGetSize.description:
Returns the size of a file in bytes.

This node returns the size in bytes of the file at the given path.
Raises an error if the path doesn't exist or isn't a file.
output_tooltips: The file size in bytes.

recursive.tooltip: When True, '**' also matches inside subdirectories.

Basic data handling: PathGlob.name: Basic data handling: PathGlob
Basic data handling: PathGlob.description:
Finds paths matching a pattern.

This node returns a list of paths matching the given pattern.
The pattern follows shell-style wildcard rules:
* - matches any number of characters
? - matches a single character
[seq] - matches any character in seq
[!seq] - matches any character not in seq
output_tooltips: All paths matching the pattern, as a data list.

Basic data handling: PathInputDir.name: Basic data handling: PathInputDir
Basic data handling: PathInputDir.description:
Returns the ComfyUI input path.

This is where input images are usually stored when using ComfyUI
output_tooltips: Absolute path of ComfyUI's input directory.

path.tooltip: Path to test.

Basic data handling: PathIsAbsolute.name: Basic data handling: PathIsAbsolute
Basic data handling: PathIsAbsolute.description:
Checks if a path is absolute.

This node returns True if the path is absolute (begins at the root directory),
and False if it's relative.
output_tooltips: True when the path is absolute (starts at the root).

path.tooltip: Path to test.

Basic data handling: PathIsDir.name: Basic data handling: PathIsDir
Basic data handling: PathIsDir.description:
Checks if a path points to a directory.

This node returns True if the path exists and is a directory,
and False otherwise.
output_tooltips: True when the path exists and is a directory.

path.tooltip: Path to test.

Basic data handling: PathIsFile.name: Basic data handling: PathIsFile
Basic data handling: PathIsFile.description:
Checks if a path points to a file.

This node returns True if the path exists and is a regular file,
and False otherwise.
output_tooltips: True when the path exists and is a regular file.

Basic data handling: PathJoin.name: Basic data handling: PathJoin
Basic data handling: PathJoin.description:
Joins multiple path components into a single path.

This node takes multiple path components and joins them intelligently
to form a single path. It handles directory separators correctly
for the operating system.
output_tooltips: The components joined into a single path.

path.tooltip: Directory to list.

files_only.tooltip: When True, only files are returned.

dirs_only.tooltip: When True, only directories are returned.

Basic data handling: PathListDir.name: Basic data handling: PathListDir
Basic data handling: PathListDir.description:
Lists the contents of a directory.

This node returns a list of files and directories in the specified path.
If 'files_only' is True, it only returns files.
If 'dirs_only' is True, it only returns directories.
If both are False, it returns all contents.
output_tooltips: The names of the directory entries, as a data list.

path.tooltip: Path to normalize.

Basic data handling: PathNormalize.name: Basic data handling: PathNormalize
Basic data handling: PathNormalize.description:
Normalizes a path.

This node normalizes a path by collapsing redundant separators,
resolving up-level references, and converting to the correct
separator for the operating system.
output_tooltips: The path with redundant separators and up-level references collapsed.

Basic data handling: PathOutputDir.name: Basic data handling: PathOutputDir
Basic data handling: PathOutputDir.description:
Returns the ComfyUI output path.

This is where output images are usually stored when using ComfyUI
output_tooltips: Absolute path of ComfyUI's output directory.

path.tooltip: Path to express relative to start.

start.tooltip: Base path; the current working directory is used when empty.

Basic data handling: PathRelative.name: Basic data handling: PathRelative
Basic data handling: PathRelative.description:
Returns a relative path.

This node computes a relative path from the 'start' path to the 'path'.
If 'start' is not provided, the current working directory is used.
output_tooltips: The path expressed relative to start.

path.tooltip: Path to split into directory and filename.

Basic data handling: PathSplit.name: Basic data handling: PathSplit
Basic data handling: PathSplit.description:
Splits a path into directory and filename components.

This node takes a path and returns a tuple containing the directory path
and the filename.
output_tooltips: The directory (head) component.
The filename (tail) component.

path.tooltip: Path to split into name and extension.

Basic data handling: PathSplitExt.name: Basic data handling: PathSplitExt
Basic data handling: PathSplitExt.description:
Splits a path into name and extension components.

This node takes a path and returns a tuple containing the path without
the extension and the extension (including the dot).
output_tooltips: The path without its extension.
The extension including the dot (empty when none).

path.tooltip: Path of the UTF-8 text file to read.

Basic data handling: PathLoadStringFile.name: Basic data handling: PathLoadStringFile
Basic data handling: PathLoadStringFile.description:
Loads a text file in UTF-8 encoding and returns its content as a STRING
without any further processing.
output_tooltips: The file content (empty when the file is missing or unreadable).
True when the file exists and was read.

path.tooltip: Path of the image file to load.

Basic data handling: PathLoadImageRGB.name: Basic data handling: PathLoadImageRGB
Basic data handling: PathLoadImageRGB.description:
Loads an image from a file path and returns only the RGB channels.

This node loads an image from the specified path and processes it to
return only the RGB channels as a tensor, ignoring any alpha channel.
output_tooltips: The RGB image as a tensor (a blank 1x1 image when the file is missing).
True when the image was loaded.

path.tooltip: Path of the image file to load.

Basic data handling: PathLoadImageRGBA.name: Basic data handling: PathLoadImageRGBA
Basic data handling: PathLoadImageRGBA.description:
Loads an image from a file path and returns RGB channels and Alpha as a mask.

This node loads an image from the specified path and processes it to
return the RGB channels as a tensor and the Alpha channel as a mask tensor.
If the image has no alpha channel, a blank mask is returned.
output_tooltips: The RGB image as a tensor.
The alpha channel as a mask (blank when the image has none).
True when the image was loaded.

path.tooltip: Path of the image whose alpha channel is used.

Basic data handling: PathLoadMaskFromAlp.name: Basic data handling: PathLoadMaskFromAlpha
Basic data handling: PathLoadMaskFromAlp.description:
Loads a mask from the alpha channel of an image.

This node loads an image from the specified path and extracts the alpha
channel to use as a mask. If the image has no alpha channel, a blank mask
is returned.
output_tooltips: The alpha channel as a mask (blank when the image has none or is missing).
True when the image was loaded.

path.tooltip: Path of the image to build the mask from.

invert.tooltip: Invert the mask (1.0 - mask) after extraction.

Basic data handling: PathLoadMaskFromGre.name: Basic data handling: PathLoadMaskFromGreyscale
Basic data handling: PathLoadMaskFromGre.description:
Loads a mask from a greyscale image or the red channel of an RGB image.

This node loads an image from the specified path and creates a mask from it.
If the image is greyscale, the intensity is used directly.
If the image is RGB, the red channel is used.
output_tooltips: The mask derived from the greyscale/red channel.
True when the image was loaded.

text.tooltip: The text to write.

path.tooltip: Destination file path.

append.tooltip: Append to an existing file instead of overwriting it.

encoding.tooltip: Text encoding to use when writing.

Basic data handling: PathSaveStringFile.name: Basic data handling: PathSaveStringFile
Basic data handling: PathSaveStringFile.description:
Saves a string to a text file.

This node takes a string and saves it to the specified path as a text file.
Optionally, you can choose to create the directory if it doesn't exist.
If 'append' is True, the text is appended to an existing file instead of
overwriting it.
output_tooltips: True when the file was written successfully.

path.tooltip: Destination file path (an extension is added from the format when missing).

format.tooltip: Image format: png, jpg, webp or jxl (jxl needs pillow-jxl installed).

quality.tooltip: Quality for lossy formats (jpg/webp/jxl).

prompt.tooltip: Optional positive prompt embedded as parameters metadata.

negative_prompt.tooltip: Optional negative prompt embedded as parameters metadata.

Basic data handling: PathSaveImageRGB.name: Basic data handling: PathSaveImageRGB
Basic data handling: PathSaveImageRGB.description:
Saves an image to a file.

This node takes an image tensor and saves it to the specified path.
Supports various image formats like PNG, JPG, WEBP, JXL (if pillow-jxl is installed), etc.

When ``prompt`` and/or ``negative_prompt`` are provided, they are embedded
into the saved image as ``parameters`` metadata: in the PNG text chunk, in
the EXIF ``UserComment`` (and ``ImageDescription`` for JPEG) fields, and in
the EXIF + XMP boxes for JPEG XL. Formats that cannot carry text metadata
ignore the prompts.
output_tooltips: True when the image was saved successfully.

path.tooltip: Destination file path (an extension is added from the format when missing).

format.tooltip: Image format supporting alpha: png, webp or jxl; jpg is coerced to png.

quality.tooltip: Quality for lossy formats (webp/jxl).

invert_mask.tooltip: Invert the mask before using it as the alpha channel.

prompt.tooltip: Optional positive prompt embedded as parameters metadata.

negative_prompt.tooltip: Optional negative prompt embedded as parameters metadata.

Basic data handling: PathSaveImageRGBA.name: Basic data handling: PathSaveImageRGBA
Basic data handling: PathSaveImageRGBA.description:
Saves an image with a mask to a file with transparency.

This node takes an image tensor and a mask tensor and saves them to the
specified path as an image with transparency, where the mask defines the
alpha channel.

When ``prompt`` and/or ``negative_prompt`` are provided, they are embedded
into the saved image as ``parameters`` metadata: in the PNG text chunk, in
the EXIF ``UserComment`` (and ``ImageDescription`` for JPEG) fields, and in
the EXIF + XMP boxes for JPEG XL. Formats that cannot carry text metadata
ignore the prompts.
output_tooltips: True when the image with alpha was saved successfully.

Basic data handling: RegexFindallDataLis.name: Basic data handling: RegexFindallDataList
Basic data handling: RegexFindallDataLis.description: Returns all non-overlapping matches of a pattern in the string as a data list of strings.
output_tooltips: Each non-overlapping match of the pattern, as a data list of strings.

Basic data handling: RegexFindallList.name: Basic data handling: RegexFindallList
Basic data handling: RegexFindallList.description: Returns all non-overlapping matches of a pattern in the string as a Python LIST.
output_tooltips: Each non-overlapping match of the pattern, as a Python LIST of strings.

pattern.tooltip: Regular expression pattern containing named groups, e.g. (?P<name>...).

Basic data handling: RegexGroupDict.name: Basic data handling: RegexGroupDict
Basic data handling: RegexGroupDict.description:
Searches the string with the given pattern and returns a DICT of named groups.
If no match is found, it returns an empty DICT.
output_tooltips: Named capture groups mapped to their matched text (empty DICT when there is no match).

pattern.tooltip: Regular expression pattern with capturing groups, e.g. (\d+)-(\d+).

Basic data handling: RegexSearchGroupsDa.name: Basic data handling: RegexSearchGroupsDataList
Basic data handling: RegexSearchGroupsDa.description:
Searches the string for a match to the pattern and returns a data list of the captured groups.
If no match is found, it returns an empty data list.
output_tooltips: The captured groups of the first match, as a data list (empty when there is no match).

pattern.tooltip: Regular expression pattern with capturing groups, e.g. (\d+)-(\d+).

Basic data handling: RegexSearchGroupsLi.name: Basic data handling: RegexSearchGroupsList
Basic data handling: RegexSearchGroupsLi.description:
Searches the string for a match to the pattern and returns a Python LIST of the captured groups.
If no match is found, it returns an empty LIST.
output_tooltips: The captured groups of the first match, as a Python LIST (empty when there is no match).

pattern.tooltip: Regular expression pattern used as the delimiter.

Basic data handling: RegexSplitDataList.name: Basic data handling: RegexSplitDataList
Basic data handling: RegexSplitDataList.description: Splits the string at each match of the pattern and returns a data list of substrings.
output_tooltips: The substrings between matches, as a data list.

pattern.tooltip: Regular expression pattern used as the delimiter.

Basic data handling: RegexSplitList.name: Basic data handling: RegexSplitList
Basic data handling: RegexSplitList.description: Splits the string at each match of the pattern and returns a Python LIST of substrings.
output_tooltips: The substrings between matches, as a Python LIST.

pattern.tooltip: Regular expression pattern whose matches are replaced.

repl.tooltip: Replacement text. Backreferences to groups are supported.

count.tooltip: Maximum number of replacements; 0 replaces all occurrences.

Basic data handling: RegexSub.name: Basic data handling: RegexSub
Basic data handling: RegexSub.description: Substitutes matches of the pattern in the string with a replacement string.
output_tooltips: The string with the matched parts replaced.

pattern.tooltip: Regular expression pattern to search for.

Basic data handling: RegexTest.name: Basic data handling: RegexTest
Basic data handling: RegexTest.description:
Tests whether a given regex pattern matches any part of the input string.
Returns True if a match is found, otherwise False.
output_tooltips: True when the pattern matches any part of the string, otherwise False.

item_0.tooltip: One of the items to add to the SET. Connect more values to add more items.

Basic data handling: SetCreate.name: Basic data handling: SetCreate
Basic data handling: SetCreate.description:
Creates a new SET from items.

This node creates and returns a SET. The list of items is dynamically
extended based on the number of inputs provided.
output_tooltips: The new SET containing the provided items (duplicates removed).

item_0.tooltip: One of the boolean items to add to the SET. Connect more values to add more items.

Basic data handling: SetCreateFromBoolea.name: Basic data handling: SetCreateFromBoolean
Basic data handling: SetCreateFromBoolea.description:
Creates a new SET from items.

This node creates and returns a SET. The list of items is dynamically
extended based on the number of inputs provided.
output_tooltips: The new SET containing the provided boolean items (duplicates removed).

item_0.tooltip: One of the float items to add to the SET. Connect more values to add more items.

Basic data handling: SetCreateFromFloat.name: Basic data handling: SetCreateFromFloat
Basic data handling: SetCreateFromFloat.description:
Creates a new SET from items.

This node creates and returns a SET. The list of items is dynamically
extended based on the number of inputs provided.
output_tooltips: The new SET containing the provided float items (duplicates removed).

item_0.tooltip: One of the integer items to add to the SET. Connect more values to add more items.

Basic data handling: SetCreateFromInt.name: Basic data handling: SetCreateFromInt
Basic data handling: SetCreateFromInt.description:
Creates a new SET from items.

This node creates and returns a SET. The list of items is dynamically
extended based on the number of inputs provided.
output_tooltips: The new SET containing the provided integer items (duplicates removed).

item_0.tooltip: One of the string items to add to the SET. Connect more values to add more items.

Basic data handling: SetCreateFromString.name: Basic data handling: SetCreateFromString
Basic data handling: SetCreateFromString.description:
Creates a new SET from items.

This node creates and returns a SET. The list of items is dynamically
extended based on the number of inputs provided.
output_tooltips: The new SET containing the provided string items (duplicates removed).

Basic data handling: SetAdd.name: Basic data handling: SetAdd
Basic data handling: SetAdd.description:
Adds an item to a SET.

This node takes a SET and any item as inputs, then returns a new SET
with the item added. If the item is already present, the SET remains unchanged.
output_tooltips: The SET with the item added (unchanged when the item was already present).

Basic data handling: SetAll.name: Basic data handling: SetAll
Basic data handling: SetAll.description:
Checks if all elements in the SET are true.

This node takes a SET as input and returns True if all elements in the SET
evaluate to True (or if the SET is empty), and False otherwise.
output_tooltips: True when every element is truthy (or the SET is empty).

Basic data handling: SetAny.name: Basic data handling: SetAny
Basic data handling: SetAny.description:
Checks if any element in the SET is true.

This node takes a SET as input and returns True if at least one element
in the SET evaluates to True, and False otherwise (including if the SET is empty).
output_tooltips: True when at least one element is truthy (False for an empty SET).

value.tooltip: The value to look for.

Basic data handling: SetContains.name: Basic data handling: SetContains
Basic data handling: SetContains.description:
Checks if a SET contains a specified value.

This node takes a SET and a value as inputs, then returns True if the value
is present in the SET, and False otherwise.
output_tooltips: True when the value is present in the SET.

set2.tooltip: The SET of elements to remove.

Basic data handling: SetDifference.name: Basic data handling: SetDifference
Basic data handling: SetDifference.description:
Returns the difference between two SETs.

This node takes two SETs as input and returns a new SET containing
elements in the first SET but not in the second SET.
output_tooltips: Elements in set1 that are not in set2.

item.tooltip: The item to remove if present.

Basic data handling: SetDiscard.name: Basic data handling: SetDiscard
Basic data handling: SetDiscard.description:
Removes an item from a SET if it is present.

This node takes a SET and any item as inputs, then returns a new SET
with the item removed. Unlike remove, no error is raised if the item is not present.
output_tooltips: The SET with the item removed (unchanged when it was absent).

start.tooltip: Index value assigned to the first element.

Basic data handling: SetEnumerate.name: Basic data handling: SetEnumerate
Basic data handling: SetEnumerate.description:
Enumerates elements in a SET.

This node takes a SET as input and returns a LIST of tuples where each tuple
contains an index and a value from the SET. The start parameter specifies the
initial index value (default is 0).

Note: Since SETs are unordered, the enumeration order is arbitrary but consistent
within a single operation.
output_tooltips: List of (index, value) pairs. Order is arbitrary but stable within one operation.

Basic data handling: SetIntersection.name: Basic data handling: SetIntersection
Basic data handling: SetIntersection.description:
Returns the intersection of two or more SETs.

This node takes multiple SETs as input and returns a new SET containing
only elements present in all input SETs.
output_tooltips: Elements present in all of the input SETs.

Basic data handling: SetIsDisjoint.name: Basic data handling: SetIsDisjoint
Basic data handling: SetIsDisjoint.description:
Checks if two SETs have no elements in common.

This node takes two SETs as input and returns True if they have no elements in common.
output_tooltips: True when the two SETs share no elements.

set2.tooltip: SET that may contain all of set1's elements.

Basic data handling: SetIsSubset.name: Basic data handling: SetIsSubset
Basic data handling: SetIsSubset.description:
Checks if set1 is a subset of set2.

This node takes two SETs as input and returns True if set1 is a subset of set2
(all elements in set1 are also in set2).
output_tooltips: True when every element of set1 is also in set2.

set2.tooltip: SET whose elements must all be in set1.

Basic data handling: SetIsSuperset.name: Basic data handling: SetIsSuperset
Basic data handling: SetIsSuperset.description:
Checks if set1 is a superset of set2.

This node takes two SETs as input and returns True if set1 is a superset of set2
(set1 contains all elements in set2).
output_tooltips: True when set1 contains every element of set2.

Basic data handling: SetLength.name: Basic data handling: SetLength
Basic data handling: SetLength.description:
Returns the number of items in a SET.

This node takes a SET as input and returns its length (number of elements) as an integer.
output_tooltips: The number of elements in the SET.

set.tooltip: The SET to pop an item from.

Basic data handling: SetPop.name: Basic data handling: SetPop
Basic data handling: SetPop.description:
Removes and returns an arbitrary item from a SET.

This node takes a SET as input and returns both the new SET
with an arbitrary item removed and the removed item.
When the SET is empty, the item is None.
output_tooltips: The SET with an arbitrary item removed.
The removed item (None when the SET was empty).

set.tooltip: The SET to pop a random element from.

seed.tooltip: Seed for reproducible selection. Leave empty to pick randomly each run.

Basic data handling: SetPopRandom.name: Basic data handling: SetPopRandom
Basic data handling: SetPopRandom.description:
Removes and returns a random element from a SET.

This node takes a SET as input and returns the SET with a random element removed
and the removed element itself. If the SET is empty, it returns None for the element.
An optional seed can be provided for reproducible selection.
output_tooltips: The SET with a random element removed.
The removed element (None when the SET was empty).

Basic data handling: SetRemove.name: Basic data handling: SetRemove
Basic data handling: SetRemove.description:
Removes an item from a SET.

This node takes a SET and any item as inputs, then returns a new SET
with the item removed and a success indicator. If the item is not present,
the original SET is returned with success set to False.
output_tooltips: The SET with the item removed.
True when the item was present and removed.

set.tooltip: The SET of numbers to sum.

start.tooltip: Initial value added to the sum.

Basic data handling: SetSum.name: Basic data handling: SetSum
Basic data handling: SetSum.description:
Calculates the sum of all elements in a SET.

This node takes a SET as input and returns the sum of all its elements.
The optional start parameter specifies the initial value (default is 0).

Note: This operation requires all elements to be numeric or otherwise
compatible with addition. If the SET contains mixed or incompatible types,
it may raise an error.
output_tooltips: The total as an integer.
The total as a float.

Basic data handling: SetSymmetricDiffere.name: Basic data handling: SetSymmetricDifference
Basic data handling: SetSymmetricDiffere.description:
Returns the symmetric difference between two SETs.

This node takes two SETs as input and returns a new SET containing
elements in either SET but not in both.
output_tooltips: Elements present in exactly one of the two SETs.

Basic data handling: SetUnion.name: Basic data handling: SetUnion
Basic data handling: SetUnion.description:
Returns the union of two or more SETs.

This node takes multiple SETs as input and returns a new SET containing
all elements from all the input SETs.
output_tooltips: All elements from every input SET (duplicates removed).

Basic data handling: SetToDataList.name: Basic data handling: SetToDataList
Basic data handling: SetToDataList.description:
Converts a SET object into a ComfyUI data list.

This node takes a SET object (Python set as a single variable) and
converts it to a ComfyUI data list, allowing its items to be processed
individually by nodes that accept data lists.
output_tooltips: The SET's elements as a ComfyUI data list.

Basic data handling: SetToList.name: Basic data handling: SetToList
Basic data handling: SetToList.description:
Converts a SET into a LIST.

This node takes a SET input and creates a new LIST containing all elements
from the SET. Note that the order of elements in the resulting LIST is arbitrary
since SETs are unordered collections.
output_tooltips: The SET's elements as a Python LIST (order is arbitrary).

value.tooltip: The number to take the absolute value of.

Basic data handling: MathAbs.name: Basic data handling: MathAbs
Basic data handling: MathAbs.description:
Returns the absolute value of a number.

This node takes a number and returns its absolute value (magnitude without sign).
output_tooltips: The absolute (non-negative) value of the input.

value.tooltip: The value (in [-1, 1]) whose arc cosine is computed.

Basic data handling: MathAcos.name: Basic data handling: MathAcos
Basic data handling: MathAcos.description:
Calculates the arc cosine (inverse cosine) of a value.

This node takes a value between -1 and 1, and returns the arc cosine in radians or degrees.
The arc cosine is the inverse operation of cosine, returning the angle whose cosine is the input value.
output_tooltips: The arc cosine angle in the chosen unit.

value.tooltip: The value (in [-1, 1]) whose arc sine is computed.

Basic data handling: MathAsin.name: Basic data handling: MathAsin
Basic data handling: MathAsin.description:
Calculates the arc sine (inverse sine) of a value.

This node takes a value between -1 and 1, and returns the arc sine in radians or degrees.
The arc sine is the inverse operation of sine, returning the angle whose sine is the input value.
output_tooltips: The arc sine angle in the chosen unit.

value.tooltip: The value whose arc tangent is computed.

Basic data handling: MathAtan.name: Basic data handling: MathAtan
Basic data handling: MathAtan.description:
Calculates the arc tangent (inverse tangent) of a value.

This node takes a value and returns the arc tangent in radians or degrees.
The arc tangent is the inverse operation of tangent, returning the angle whose tangent is the input value.
output_tooltips: The arc tangent angle in the chosen unit.

Basic data handling: MathAtan2.name: Basic data handling: MathAtan2
Basic data handling: MathAtan2.description:
Calculates the arc tangent of y/x, considering the quadrant.

This node takes y and x coordinates and returns the arc tangent in radians or degrees.
Unlike atan(y/x), this function handles the case where x is zero and correctly determines
the quadrant of the resulting angle.
output_tooltips: The angle of the point (x, y) in the chosen unit.

value.tooltip: The number to round up.

Basic data handling: MathCeil.name: Basic data handling: MathCeil
Basic data handling: MathCeil.description:
Returns the ceiling of a number.

This node takes a number and returns the smallest integer greater than or equal to the input value.
output_tooltips: The smallest integer greater than or equal to the value.

angle.tooltip: The angle to take the cosine of.

Basic data handling: MathCos.name: Basic data handling: MathCos
Basic data handling: MathCos.description:
Calculates the cosine of an angle in radians or degrees.

This node takes an angle value and unit type, and returns the cosine of that angle.
The cosine of an angle is the ratio of the length of the adjacent side to the length
of the hypotenuse in a right-angled triangle.

Basic data handling: MathFormula.name: Basic data handling: MathFormula
Basic data handling: MathFormula.description:
A node that evaluates a mathematical formula provided as a string without using eval.

This node takes an arbitrary number of numerical inputs (single letters like `a`, `b`, `c`, etc.) and safely
evaluates the formula with supported operations: +, -, *, /, //, %, **, parentheses, and mathematical
functions.

NOTE on Operator Precedence: This parser uses standard precedence rules. Unary minus binds tightly,
so expressions like `-a ** 2` are interpreted as `(-a) ** 2`. To calculate `-(a ** 2)`,
use parentheses: `-(a ** 2)`.

The identifiers `e` and `pi` are special. When used as a function call (`e()`, `pi()`), they return their
respective mathematical constants. When used as a variable (`e`), they expect a corresponding input.

Supported functions:
- Basic: abs, floor, ceil, round, min(a,b), max(a,b)
- Trigonometric: sin, cos, tan, asin, acos, atan, atan2(y,x), degrees, radians
- Hyperbolic: sinh, cosh, tanh, asinh, acosh, atanh
- Exponential & Logarithmic: exp, log, log10, log2, sqrt, pow(base,exp)
- Constants (must be called with empty parentheses): pi(), e()
output_tooltips: The numerical result of evaluating the formula.

This node uses the [deep bump](https://github.com/HugoTini/DeepBump) model (GPLv3).
The 3 inference modes (color -> normals, normals -> curvature, normals -> depth) are all baked into a single node with a dropdown to select the operation.

Get Batch From History (mtb).name: Get Batch From History (mtb)
Get Batch From History (mtb).description:
# Get Batch from History This experimental node does something really simple, it reads the outputs from the history endpoint of Comfy. Outputs gets populated by... output nodes. There are various ones but for instance in core comfy, `Save Image` and `Preview Image` are output nodes. I advice to start simple and have workflows that only generates one output per queue run. Of course once you master it you can use multiple outputs as output order is kept (as long as all outputs are ran). Another basic use case of batch from history that you can see in the 4th [example](Examples), the fake deforum effect, basically this flow allows you to **feedback** an image using the history. A classic example when showing the feedback concept is the poor man's [grey scott diffusion model](https://groups.csail.mit.edu/mac/projects/amorphous/GrayScott/) i.e the "creative" derivative using only a gaussian blur and a sharp at each fed steps. Stack Images (mtb).name: Stack Images (mtb)
Stack Images (mtb).description:
# Stack Images

A simple way to stack images either horizontally or vertically. Stack image uses [dynamic inputs](web-dynamic-inputs).

It outputs RGBA tensors and supports RGB or RGBA as input (normalized to RGBA internally). If the image dimensions don't match they must at least match:
- in `width` when stacking vertically.
- in `height` when stacking horizontally.

Here is an example workflow using [Text To Image](nodes-text-to-image) (the text was generated using [Nous Hermes 2 Vision](https://huggingface.co/billborkowski/llava-NousResearch_Nous-Hermes-2-Vision-GGUF) thanks to the great [ComfyUI_VLM_nodes](https://github.com/gokayfem/ComfyUI_VLM_nodes) extension. For simplicity's sake, the workflow doesn't contain external nodes:

![stack_images](https://github.com/melMass/comfy_mtb/assets/7041726/a0c03621-3377-46cf-a6b4-f47e70c7d11f)

Postshot Train (mtb).name: Postshot Train (mtb)
Postshot Train (mtb).description:
# Postshot Train

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fcaf4163-28c7-4768-a785-bc794fca3ec0


Wrapper around the [Potshot](https://www.jawset.com/) CLI. 
You must first run the GUI at least once and login.
If you use a custom install location you can specify it in **Settings > MTB**



## Radiance Field Profile

Postshot supports two different models to create radiance fields:
- Gaussian Splatting (Splat)
- Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF).

### Splat MCMC

Both Splat profiles allow for very fast rendering and quickly reconstruct fine detail in well-covered regions of the scene.

The Splat MCMC profile is currently the recommended profile for most scenes. It allows limiting the number of Splat primitives and thereby the amount of memory and disk space the resulting model requires.

### Splat ADC

The Splat ADC profile is very similar to the Splat MCMC profile, but differs in the way it produces detail in the scene during training. You can control the amount of detail it creates during training through the Splat Density parameter.

### NeRF models

When using the NeRF model, the maximum accuracy has to be specified before the training can begin. Postshot currently provides five sizes (S, M, L, XL, XXL) for NeRF models. NeRFs are much slower to render than Splats.

Here is an intuition for how 'large' the NeRF profile options are:
- **S** is for toy-like testing.
- **M** is a significant step up, such that real scenes can be reasonably captured with low memory requirements.
- **L** is the recommended default if you want to produce good image quality.
- **XL** and **XXL** are for pushing toward fine detail in the scene center or for large scenes.

Transform Image (mtb).name: Transform Image (mtb)
Transform Image (mtb).description:
# Transform Image

Transform images while maintaining the input tensor shape

## Filter Types
1. `NEAREST`: Nearest neighbor - fastest but lowest quality
2. `BOX`: Box filtering - similar to nearest neighbor but with some averaging
3. `BILINEAR`: Bilinear filtering - good balance between quality and speed
4. `HAMMING`: Hamming filtering - improved version of bilinear (doesn't allow rotations)
5. `BICUBIC`: Bicubic filtering - better quality than bilinear but slower
6. `LANCZOS`: Lanczos filtering - highest quality but slowest (doesn't allow rotations)

# Load Image Sequence

Load an image sequence from a folder. The current frame is used to determine which image to load.  
The UX need improvements but you can use it as follow:  

- If current_frame is -1, it will load all the frames matching the pattern.
- If the path contains a `*` it will glob the paths using it.
- If range is provided (for instance `0-10` to load frame 0 to 10) current_frame is ignored.

LoadVideoFromUrl.name: LoadVideoFromUrl
LoadVideoFromUrl.description:
Load Video (Path) 🎥🅥🅗🅢
Loads a video from an arbitrary path
[-]
Inputs:
[-]
meta_batch: (optional) Connect to a Meta Batch manager to divide extremely long sequences into sub batches. See the documentation for Meta Batch Manager
[-]
vae: (optional) If provided the node will output latents instead of images. This drastically reduces the required RAM (not VRAM) when working with long (100+ frames) sequences
Using this is strongly encouraged unless connecting to a node that requires a blue image connection such as Apply Controllnet
[-]
Outputs:
[-]
IMAGE: The loaded images
[-]
frame_count: The length of images just returned
[-]
audio: The audio from the loaded video
[-]
video_info: Exposes additional info about the video such as the source frame rate, or the total length
[-]
LATENT: The loaded images pre-converted to latents. Only available when a vae is connected
[-]
Widgets:
[-]
video: The video file to be loaded.
You can also select an image to load it as a single frame
This is a VHS_PATH input. When edited, it provides a list of possible valid files or directories
The current top-most completion may be selected with Tab
You can navigate up a directory by pressing Ctrl+B (or Ctrl+W if supported by browser)
The filter on suggested file types can be disabled by pressing Ctrl+G.
If converted to an input, this functions as a string
[-]
force_rate: Drops or duplicates frames so that the produced output has the target frame rate. Many motion models are trained on videos of a specific frame rate and will give better results if input matches that frame rate. If set to 0, all frames are returned. May give unusual results with inputs that have a variable frame rate like animated gifs. Reducing this value can also greatly reduce the execution time and memory requirements.
[-]
force_size: Previously was used to provide suggested resolutions. Instead, custom_width and custom_height can be disabled by setting to 0.
[-]
custom_width: Allows for an arbitrary width to be entered, cropping to maintain aspect ratio if both are set
[-]
custom_height: Allows for an arbitrary height to be entered, cropping to maintain aspect ratio if both are set
[-]
frame_load_cap: The maximum number of frames to load. If 0, all frames are loaded.
[-]
skip_first_frames: A number of frames which are discarded before producing output.
[-]
select_every_nth: Similar to frame rate. Keeps only the first of every n frames and discard the rest. Has better compatibility with variable frame rate inputs such as gifs. When combined with force_rate, select_every_nth_applies after force_rate so the resulting output has a frame rate equivalent to force_rate/select_every_nth. select_every_nth does not apply to skip_first_frames
[-]
format: Updates other widgets so that only values supported by the given format can be entered and provides recommended defaults.
[-]
videopreview: Displays a preview for the selected video input. Will only be shown if Advanced Previews is enabled. This preview will reflect the frame_load_cap, force_rate, skip_first_frames, and select_every_nth values chosen. If the video has audio, it will also be previewed when moused over. Additional preview options can be accessed with right click.

AV_FaceDetailer.name: AV_FaceDetailer
AV_FaceDetailer.description:
This node enhances details by automatically detecting specific objects in the input image using detection models (bbox, segm, sam) and regenerating the image by enlarging the detected area based on the guide size.
Although this node is specialized to simplify the commonly used facial detail enhancement workflow, it can also be used for various automatic inpainting purposes depending on the detection model.

resolution_preset.description: Target visual resolution / pixel budget. Pick either a standard resolution label or an optimized megapixel tier.

no_scale.description: Bypass all calculations and output the source dimensions exactly.

scale_from_image.description: IMAGE ASPECT ignores the aspect controls below and uses the connected image shape. USE ASPECT BELOW uses the visible aspect controls.

aspect_preset_when_not_image.description: Used only when scale_from_image is USE ASPECT BELOW. Ignored while IMAGE ASPECT is selected.

swap_aspect_when_not_image.description: Used only when scale_from_image is USE ASPECT BELOW. Flip width and height.

custom_aspect_width.description: Used only when scale_from_image is USE ASPECT BELOW and aspect preset is CUSTOM. Ratio width, not final pixels.

custom_aspect_height.description: Used only when scale_from_image is USE ASPECT BELOW and aspect preset is CUSTOM. Ratio height, not final pixels.

mode.description: Snapping engine. Use WAN/LTX (Div32) for modern video models.

image.description: The source image used to calculate the target aspect ratio.

DaSiWa_ResolutionScaleCalculator.name: DaSiWa_ResolutionScaleCalculator
DaSiWa_ResolutionScaleCalculator.description:
DaSiWa Resolution Scale Calculator
    
    Calculates mathematically precise resolutions based on a target Megapixel area.
    
    - Standard Mode: Pure mathematical scaling.

    - WAN/LTX Mode: Snaps to 32-pixel boundaries (mandatory for WAN/LTX VAEs).

    - No Scale: Overrides all math and outputs the source image dimensions directly.

size_mode.description: Choose whether to scale by a factor or resize into a target width and height.

aspect_mode.description: How a target resolution handles the source aspect ratio. Multiplier always preserves it.

target_width.description: Target box width. Used in Target resolution mode.

target_height.description: Target box height. Used in Target resolution mode.

scale_multiplier.description: Scale factor. Used in Multiplier mode.

divisible_by.description: Floor output dimensions to this multiple.

DaSiWa_TorchResize.name: DaSiWa_TorchResize
DaSiWa_TorchResize.description: Dependency-free PyTorch batch resize for ComfyUI images. Supports pixel-perfect nearest, bilinear, bicubic, area, and cached separable Lanczos resampling.

enabled.description: Master toggle to activate or deactivate the switch.

trigger_on.description: Define if the switch is active when the boolean is True or False.

action.description: Choose whether to Mute (stop execution) or Bypass (pass through) targets.

DaSiWa_NodeStatusSwitch.name: DaSiWa_NodeStatusSwitch
DaSiWa_NodeStatusSwitch.description: DaSiWa Node Status Switch: mutes or bypasses connected target nodes based on a boolean state, with an enabled output for chaining switches.

images.description: Input image or video batch to process.

denoise.description: Enable NVIDIA RTX Denoise pass to clean up image grain and noise.

denoise_quality.description: Quality tier for the Denoise pass. Higher tiers use more GPU compute.

deblur.description: Enable NVIDIA RTX Deblur pass to reduce motion or focus blur.

deblur_quality.description: Quality tier for the Deblur pass.

upscale.description:
Upscale Mode:
- VSR: Standard AI upscaling.
- High Bitrate: Optimized for heavily compressed/noisy sources.
- Off: Skip scaling.

upscale_quality.description: Quality tier for the Upscale pass.

resize_type.description:
Target Size Logic:
- Same Size: Keep original dimensions.
- Scale: Multiply resolution by 'scale'.
- Keep Ratio: Match 'megapixels' while keeping original shape.
- Preset Ratio: Match 'megapixels' but force to 'ratio_preset'.
- Manual: Exact pixels.

scale.description: Multiplier for resolution (used by 'Scale' type). 2.0 = 4x the total pixels.

megapixels.description: Target total area in millions of pixels (used by Ratio types).

divisible_by.description: Snaps final resolution to a multiple of this value. Use 8 to match RTX VSR; choose 32 only when a downstream video model requires it.

resize_method.description: Mismatch handling: 'Crop' fills the target area, 'Letterbox' fits inside with black bars.

device_id.description: GPU Index for RTX VFX computation.

empty_cache.description: Run a lightweight GC + empty_cache before allocation; also calls model_management.soft_empty_cache() to ask ComfyUI models to unload, which can free VRAM but may slow subsequent nodes.

use_mmap.description: OFF (default): never use disk — the output is allocated lazily in memory (VRAM when it fits, otherwise RAM) and the kernel decides, like the reference NVIDIA node. **WARN:** enable this ONLY for very long video batches that genuinely exceed available RAM; when on, disk is used as the last tier of the VRAM -> RAM -> disk chain and a multi-giB .mmap temp file is written to your temp drive for the whole run.

auto_unload_models.description: When VRAM/RAM is insufficient for the output, automatically unload ComfyUI-managed models (like the manual 'empty cache' but a full unload) and re-check before falling back to disk. Off: skip the unload and fall back directly.

DaSiWa_RTX_UpscalerRefiner.name: DaSiWa_RTX_UpscalerRefiner
DaSiWa_RTX_UpscalerRefiner.description:
DaSiWa RTX Upscaler & Refiner: A high-performance 3-pass processing node.
1. Refine Pass: Runs at source resolution to clean up noise or blur using NVIDIA RTX VFX.
2. Upscale Pass: Scales the image up to 4x using VSR or High Bitrate modes.
Processes frame-by-frame to maintain low VRAM usage for video batches.

watermark_path.description: Select the watermark file (PNG recommended for transparency).

position.description: Static placement, or starting placement when randomize_position is enabled.

scale.description: Size relative to image width (0.2 = 20% width).

resampling.description: Scaling filter used when resizing the watermark. Bicubic is smooth; nearest keeps hard pixel edges.

padding_x.description: Horizontal inset from the selected edge, in pixels.

padding_y.description: Vertical inset from the selected edge, in pixels.

optical_padding.description: Adjust placement by the watermark's visual center (useful for wide/rotated marks).

optical_strength.description: Strength of optical-padding correction. 0 disables correction; 1 applies the full visual-center offset.

random_switches.description: Number of times to switch position when randomize_position is enabled.

fade.description: Enable fade in at start and end.

fade_margin.description: Fade duration as a percentage of total frames (0.1 = 10%).

randomize_position.description: Cycle through corner positions, starting at the selected position.

random_seed.description: 0 derives a stable seed from the watermark file name.

DaSiWa_Watermark.name: DaSiWa_Watermark
DaSiWa_Watermark.description:
DaSiWa Watermark: A professional-grade watermark overlay node with stable CPU compositing.
Stores output batches in RAM and blends from initialized source frames to avoid flicker,
Bicubic/Lanczos scaling, rotation, and 'Optical Padding' for perfect visual alignment.

DyPE_FLUX.name: DyPE_FLUX
DyPE_FLUX.description: Applies DyPE (Dynamic Position Extrapolation) to a models for ultra-high-resolution generation.

model.tooltip: The model to patch with SEGA.

width.tooltip: Target image width. Must match the width of your empty latent.

height.tooltip: Target image height. Must match the height of your empty latent.

model_type.tooltip: Specify the model architecture. 'auto' usually works.

method.tooltip: SEGA = NTK base + spectral per-dim mscale. NTK = base NTK only (no spectral).

mscale_alpha.tooltip: SEGA amplitude. Controls how much spectral redistribution is applied.

mscale_beta.tooltip: SEGA tanh sharpness. Higher = more binary redistribution.

spread_alpha.tooltip: Non-linear mapping exponent for spread schedule.

base_mscale_formula.tooltip: power_res: m_ref = s^kappa. log_res: m_ref = 1 + kappa*ln(s).

base_mscale_coefficient.tooltip: Kappa coefficient for base mscale. Paper uses 0.08.

base_shift.tooltip: Advanced: Base shift for the noise schedule (mu).

max_shift.tooltip: Advanced: Max shift for the noise schedule (mu) at high resolutions.

output_tooltips: The model patched with SEGA.
SEGA.name: SEGA
SEGA.description: Spectral-Energy Guided Attention for ultra-high-resolution generation. Computes per-dimension RoPE mscale from the latent's Fourier spectrum.

model.tooltip: The model to patch with SPA.

width.tooltip: Target image width. Must match the width of your empty latent.

height.tooltip: Target image height. Must match the height of your empty latent.

model_type.tooltip: Specify the model architecture. 'auto' usually works.

enable_spa.tooltip: Enable or disable SPA. When disabled, the base RoPE is emitted unchanged.

bundle_size.tooltip: SPA bundle size N (HRDiT paper): tokens per bundle. 0 = auto (minimal compression that keeps every bundled position in-distribution). 1 = off (plain passthrough). 2..8 = explicit (paper recommends 3 at 2K, 5 at 4K). While the grid is inside the model's trained extent (e.g. <= 1024px) SPA is automatically a no-op. Explicit N is floored by the in-distribution minimum so bundled positions never go out of distribution; the averaged-pass count is capped at 15. A single shared bundle size is used for BOTH axes so non-square images keep their aspect ratio (no horizontal squish). Legacy values >= 32 (old group_num semantics) are treated as auto with a warning.

spa_start_sigma.tooltip: Optional sigma-threshold gate (AND-combined with spa_steps): SPA runs only while the current sigma is ABOVE this threshold. 1.0 = no sigma gating (default). Lower values make later steps run at baseline speed.

spa_steps.tooltip: Step gating (HRDiT applies SPA only on leading denoising steps): number of LEADING steps on which SPA is active. 3 = HRDiT default (recommended speed/quality tradeoff). 0 = active on every step (backward compatible, slower). A new generation (sigma jump-up) resets the counter. Later steps run plain attention at baseline speed.

spa_layer_filter.tooltip: Per-layer SPA filter (HRDiT set_spa_filter): restrict the averaged-pass SPA to a subset of transformer layers. Flat layer-index spec: '0-18,38-57' (inclusive ranges, comma-separated) or a single index '3'. Empty = every layer (default). Filtered-out layers run plain attention; the layer counter and HAP are unaffected. Invalid specs raise an error.

proportional_attention.tooltip: HRDiT proportional attention scaling: scales the attention logits by sqrt(ln(seq_len)/ln(train_seq_len)) to compensate entropy dilution on long sequences. Exact no-op at/below the trained extent (1024px). Off by default (bit-identical to previous behaviour). Either the SPA or the HAP node may enable it.

output_tooltips: The model patched with SPA.
SPA.name: SPA
SPA.description: Spatial Position Alignment (HRDiT). Prevents high-resolution spatial disorder by bundling + averaging RoPE positions. Static, no timestep dependence.

model.tooltip: The model to patch with HAP.

scope_plan_path.tooltip: Path to the scope-plan JSON (per-layer, per-head alpha/beta). Relative paths resolve against the ComfyUI-DyPE folder. Default ships the reference FLUX plan (57 layers x 24 heads). Generate a plan for your model/resolution with the 'HAP Calibrate' node or calibration/calibrate_hap.py. Ignored when a scope_plan is linked.

model_type.tooltip: Specify the model architecture. 'auto' usually works.

enable_hap.tooltip: Enable or disable HAP. When disabled, the model is returned unchanged.

scope_plan.tooltip: Calibrated scope plan linked from the 'HAP Calibrate' node. When connected, it OVERRIDES scope_plan_path — no file needed.

anchor_stride.tooltip: Global anchor blocks: every N-th image block is visible to all queries (keeps global coherence under pruning). 32 = HRDiT default. 0 = off.

text_len.tooltip: Number of leading text tokens (always fully attended). 512 = FLUX convention. When SPA is also active, the boundary is derived from the position ids and this is only a fallback.

proportional_attention.tooltip: HRDiT proportional attention scaling: scales the attention logits by sqrt(ln(seq_len)/ln(train_seq_len)) to compensate entropy dilution on long sequences. Exact no-op at/below the trained extent (1024px). Off by default (bit-identical to previous behaviour). Either the SPA or the HAP node may enable it.

output_tooltips: The model patched with HAP.
HAP.name: HAP
HAP.description: Head-Adaptive attention Pruning (HRDiT). Block-sparse attention from a calibrated scope plan — restores speed at high resolution. Combine with SPA for full HRDiT.

model.tooltip: The model to calibrate. Must be the SAME model + resolution you will run HAP on. Do NOT connect a HAP-patched model (calibrate unpruned).

positive.tooltip: Positive conditioning (from a CLIP Text Encode node). Keep it representative of your typical prompts. The same conditioning is used for every calibration prompt; each prompt index varies the noise seed.

negative.tooltip: Negative conditioning (from a CLIP Text Encode node).

width.tooltip: Calibration resolution width. Calibrate at <= 2K (memory); reuse the plan at higher resolutions.

height.tooltip: Calibration resolution height. Calibrate at <= 2K (memory); reuse the plan at higher resolutions.

num_prompts.tooltip: Number of calibration prompts to actually run (first N of the list). Paper: 30. More prompts = better averaging but longer calibration.

num_scopes.tooltip: Candidate scopes N_scope. Paper: 50. More scopes = finer granularity but slower solver.

budget_ratio.tooltip: Attention cost ratio r_c (fraction of full attention compute retained). Paper: 0.1. Lower = faster but more pruning.

chunk.tooltip: Query rows per calibration chunk (memory knob; result-invariant). Lower = less VRAM but slower.

text_len.tooltip: Number of leading text tokens (never pruned). 512 = FLUX convention.

anchor_stride.tooltip: Global anchor blocks in the cost model. 32 = HRDiT default. 0 = off.

calib_sigma.tooltip: Denoising sigma at which the single calibration step runs. 1.0 = first step (max noise). Lower values probe mid-trajectory behaviour.

seed.tooltip: Noise seed base (prompt i uses seed + i).

loss_type.tooltip: Calibration loss. 'output_norm' = MSE of the denoised prediction vs zero (no external data needed). 'reference_mse' = MSE vs a reference latent (connect the reference_latent input).

run.tooltip: Master switch. False = return empty plan without running (for safe graph wiring).

prompts.tooltip: Calibration prompts, one per line. Empty = built-in default list (5 prompts). Paper uses 30.

prompts_file.tooltip: Optional text file with one prompt per line (overrides the 'prompts' input). Relative paths resolve against the ComfyUI-DyPE folder.

reference_latent.tooltip: Target latent for 'reference_mse' loss (e.g. an encoded real image). Only needed when loss_type='reference_mse'.

output_name.tooltip: JSON file name inside <output>/dype_hap/. The written file is also loadable by the HAP node's scope_plan_path.

purge_between_prompts.tooltip: Run gc + VRAM cache purge between calibration prompts (low-VRAM cards). Slower; results identical.

output_tooltips: Validated scope plan dict — link into the HAP node's scope_plan input.
Absolute path of the written JSON (also usable in HAP's scope_plan_path).
Human-readable calibration report.

HAPCalibrate.description: Calibrates a per-head HAP scope plan for this model + resolution. Calibrate once per model+resolution; reuse the plan for all subsequent generations.

MiniMaxH3PromptBuilder.name: MiniMaxH3PromptBuilder
MiniMaxH3PromptBuilder.description: Guided prompt builder for MiniMax H3 (T2VA / I2VA / FL2VA / L2VA / full-reference). Click 'Edit prompt' on the node to open the editor. Outputs the final prompt STRING plus a pass-through for every reference slot, so media can carry on to MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo. Each media output prefers its own input, falling back to the matching item from a connected Media Loader 'references' bundle. A RefMod Stack wired to 'mods' shows its labels in the editor and passes through to the 'mods' output for RefMod Text Encode.

MiniMaxH3MediaLoader.name: MiniMaxH3MediaLoader
MiniMaxH3MediaLoader.description: Load MiniMax H3 reference media by drag-and-drop or file picker. Wire 'references' to the Prompt Builder, and to the Reference Splitter when you also want individual slots for MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo. A video's soundtrack can be split off and paired with it automatically.

MiniMaxH3ReferenceSplitter.name: MiniMaxH3ReferenceSplitter
MiniMaxH3ReferenceSplitter.description: Split a MiniMax H3 references bundle into individual picture / video / video_audio / audio slots for MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo.
